# implement.py parent ignores do-not-delegate and leaves stale worktree branches

## Problem statement

The global implement skill's parent phase (`implement.py parent`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) has two gaps that make an epic loop when a child is externally blocked: it selects `do-not-delegate`-tagged children as implementable (so every dispatch re-attempts a guarded child), and a failed/aborted `start` leaves the child's feature branch behind so every subsequent `start` fails with a cryptic "Failed to create worktree" error.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers (herdr downtime worker)** that run `implement.py parent <epic>` unattended — they need guarded children skipped and reported, not re-attempted on every cycle.
- **Operators** running `implement.py start` / `implement.py abort` on a child — they need a clear stale-branch diagnostic with a recovery path instead of a generic failure.
- Example story: *As the herdr dispatcher, when an epic's only remaining startable child is `do-not-delegate` (externally blocked), `implement.py parent` reports it as guarded and starts the next genuinely startable sibling — or stops cleanly reporting "no startable child" — rather than re-selecting the guarded child.*
- Example story: *As an operator whose earlier `start` aborted, re-running `implement.py start <child>` either resumes cleanly from the existing branch or tells me exactly which stale branch to delete.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Parent skips guarded children.** `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (e.g. `skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (e.g. `"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking. Guarded children are never started, claimed, or re-attempted by `parent`; startable siblings still proceed.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit override still works.** Direct `implement.py start <child>` / `drive <child>` on a `do-not-delegate` child continues to work (that explicit invocation is the documented override); only automatic parent recursion is gated.
- [ ] **AC3 — Stale branch handled actionably.** When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command. `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures.
- [ ] **AC4 — Failed/aborted start leaves no stale branch.** A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover: `_classify_child` / `_next_child_to_implement` with `do-not-delegate` children (guarded skipped, siblings still selected, override path unaffected) and `git_worktree_add` / `phase_start` stale-branch handling (reuse, fast-forward, actionable error, cleanup). Existing parent-recursion/dependency test suites still pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (parent-phase and abort sections) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` document guarded-child reporting and stale-branch reuse/recovery, including code comments for the new classification action.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Agent-infrastructure code owned by this repository: all edits land in `skill/implement/` here; never edit the installed copy (`~/.pi/agent/skills/...`) or an AI_Hell worktree.
- Idempotence: re-running `implement.py parent` must not create duplicate branches, duplicate worktrees, or duplicate comments, and must not reset a guarded child's status/stage.
- Never clobber another agent's in-progress claim (existing `skip-in-progress` behaviour is preserved).
- Guardedness must be distinguishable from dependency-blocking in the report so operators can see *why* a child did not start.
- The branch-cleanup path must never delete the only copy of a child's commits (no blind `git branch -D`).
- Do not relax the existing main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, or code-freeze gate.

## Existing state

- `_classify_child` (implement.py ~line 872) returns only `skip-terminal`, `skip-in-progress`, or `implement`; it inspects `status` and `deletedBy` only — it never looks at `tags`. `wl show <id> --children --json` does expose each child's `tags`, so `do-not-delegate` is readable without new plumbing.
- `_next_child_to_implement` (~line 963) and the `phase_parent` child loop (~line 5730+) both rely on `_classify_child`, so a single classification change propagates to both.
- `git_worktree_add` (~line 1826) runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> <parent_branch>` and returns a bare `bool`; `git worktree add -b` fails when the branch already exists.
- `phase_start` (~line 4254) reuses an existing worktree via `_is_worktree` (SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) but, when no worktree exists and the branch does, it reports `Failed to create worktree at ...` and only resets status to `open` — the branch survives.
- `phase_abort` (~line 5406) calls `_remove_worktree` (which removes the directory but never the branch), so the branch survives an abort and poisons the next `start`.
- No `do-not-delegate` handling exists anywhere in `implement.py` today (grep confirms); the herdr dispatcher honours the tag, the implement parent phase does not.
- Sibling item `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` (completed) already added parent-branch (`dev`) refresh before worktree creation (step 6.5 `_sync_parent_branch`); this item concerns the *child* branch already existing, which that work does not address.

## Desired change

1. Add `do-not-delegate` awareness to `_classify_child`, surface it as a distinct action in the `phase_parent` report, and skip those children in both selection paths.
2. Make `phase_start`/`git_worktree_add` branch-aware: detect an existing child branch, reuse it when safe (identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch), otherwise fail with the branch name and recovery command.
3. Clean up the branch a failed `start` created, and delete the abandoned branch on `phase_abort` when it is safe to do so.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent` (classification report + child loop), `git_worktree_add`, `phase_start` (step 7 worktree creation), `phase_abort`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document guarded-child behaviour and stale-branch recovery
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reference documentation for the new classification action and branch handling
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_loop.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` — existing parent-phase suites to extend
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`, `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py` — existing start/abort suites to extend for stale-branch handling

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — `implement.py parent` ignores the `do-not-delegate` tag when selecting the next child (open). The `do-not-delegate`-only subset of this item, retained to preserve the original report; its description states it should be closed as duplicate/absorbed once this item is resolved.
- **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1** — `implement.py finish` leaves local `dev` behind after pushing to remote `dev` (completed). Related theme: stale base for the *next* child; that item fixed the parent-branch refresh, not the child-branch-already-exists failure.
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — Implement skill safety gate should account for git worktrees (completed). Related worktree lifecycle work; different gate (dirty-tree safety), no overlap with either gap here.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — idempotent `start` that reuses an existing worktree (referenced in code); this item extends that idempotence to the branch-already-exists-no-worktree case.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (override semantics):** "unless explicitly overridden" means a direct `implement.py start`/`drive <child>` invocation, which remains the escape hatch; `parent` gets no override flag. If a `parent`-level override flag is wanted, that is an addition, not a change to AC1/AC2.
- **Risk — branch reuse ambiguity:** a stale branch may contain real partial work. Mitigation: reuse only when identical to or fast-forwardable from the parent branch; otherwise fail with instructions and never auto-delete commits.
- **Risk — false guard detection:** if the tag is written differently in another worklog (e.g. a boolean field rather than a `tags` entry), classification could miss it. Mitigation: read the same shape the herdr dispatcher uses (`tags` contains `do-not-delegate`) and add a test fixture pinning that shape.
- **Risk — scope creep into herdr:** the dispatcher's own selection logic is out of scope; this item covers `implement.py` only.
- **Risk — parent stalls silently:** if every remaining child is guarded, `parent` must report "no startable child (N guarded)" rather than a bare "nothing to do". Covered by AC1's report requirement.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the relocated report (`relocated-from:AH-0MUVRNAU5005PEUE`) already states the problem, expected behaviour, and scope, and code inspection of `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` confirmed every claim (classification paths, `git_worktree_add`'s `-b` flag, `phase_start` failure handling, `phase_abort` branch retention). One design reading is recorded as an assumption under **Risks & assumptions** ("explicitly overridden" = direct `start`/`drive` of the child).

- Q (self-resolved): "Does `wl show --children --json` expose child tags so `do-not-delegate` is detectable?" — Answer (Map): Yes; the child dict carries `tags`, and existing local worklog data stores the tag as `"tags":["do-not-delegate"]`. Source: `worklog-data.jsonl` inspection + `wl update --help` (`--do-not-delegate` flag).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the stale-branch failure already fixed by the parent-branch refresh?" — Answer (Map): No; `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` refreshes the parent branch (`dev`) before worktree creation, but `git worktree add -b` still fails when the child's own branch already exists. Source: `phase_start` step 6.5 / step 7 code.

## Related work (automated report, find-related)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MM8SJKC31N0PQ55** – Resolve stale container-dispatch branches and close associated work items (completed) — directly relevant: prior branch-staleness incident and its manual cleanup.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** – Audit: parent-first child pass-through (audit parent only first) (completed) — parent-phase traversal behaviour.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** – implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain (completed) — origin of the parent recursion this item modifies.

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abort, branch, child, classify, delegate, guarded, parent, stale, startable, worktree
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: branch, child, classify, guarded, parent, worktree (audit's parent recursion shares classification vocabulary)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: branch, child, classify, guarded, parent, worktree

# SorraAgents: decide fate of untracked `skill/pane-triage`

**Headline:** Make the deployed `pane-triage` global skill a tracked, hygiene-compliant member of `SorraAgents/skill` (Option A) instead of leaving it as a locally-excluded untracked copy, so `/skill:pane-triage` is reproducible from a fresh clone and the skill inventory, description-hygiene, and context-budget gates all agree.

## Problem Statement

The SorraAgents main checkout carries a **permanently untracked**
`skill/pane-triage/` directory (locally excluded via `.git/info/exclude`) that is
a deployed copy of the tracked `skill/pane-triage/` in ContextHub. Because
`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, this copy is what makes
`/skill:pane-triage` available to every pi session, yet it is invisible to a
fresh clone, is excluded from the skill inventory/budget, and (before the
untracked-dir isolation work) failed the hygiene and context-budget gates. A
decision is required: make the skill a first-class tracked global skill in
SorraAgents, or remove the copy.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — relies on `/skill:pane-triage` to review and close
  idle herdr panes; a removal would silently retire the skill for every
  framework project whose global skills resolve to `SorraAgents/skill`.
  - *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to keep working after a fresh
    `git clone` of SorraAgents, so my pane-cleanup workflow is reproducible on
    any machine.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the global skill inventory, description
  hygiene, and startup context-budget gate to reflect reality, so an untracked
  directory cannot hide a skill or skew the counts.
  - *As a maintainer, I want every global skill tracked in SorraAgents, so the
    hygiene tests, context-budget thresholds, and install script agree on the
    same skill set.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The skill is tracked.** `git ls-files skill/pane-triage` in the SorraAgents
   repository lists `SKILL.md`, `__init__.py`, `scripts/pane-triage.py`,
   `scripts/pane_triage.py`, and `tests/test_pane_triage.py`; the
   `skill/pane-triage/` entry is removed from `.git/info/exclude`; a fresh
   checkout of `dev` contains `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md`.
2. **Doc hygiene passes.** `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` passes
   `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py` (no legacy `skill/<name>/` references
   and no CWD-relative script invocations — commands use
   `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...`) and
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` (frontmatter description ≤140 chars,
   contains "Use when", starts with an action word). `pane-triage` is added to
   `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` in `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` (it creates or
   updates no work items, so it must not carry the standardized-report final
   step).
3. **Inventory and budget agree.** The expectations in
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` are updated for the new tracked
   skill count and total-prose budget (and the reduction-baseline exclusions, if
   applicable); `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is regenerated with
   `--include-hidden`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md` records a dated bump note
   with justification.
4. **Source parity (no drift).** The ContextHub source `skill/pane-triage/`
   receives the same hygiene edits so the deployed copy and the source do not
   diverge; the tracking/deployment model is documented in
   `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` (ContextHub).
5. **Verification.** The targeted hygiene/context-budget tests
   (`test_skill_description_hygiene.py`, `test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`,
   `test_skill_path_conventions.py`, `test_context_budget_gate.py`,
   `test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py`) pass with the directory tracked, and
   the context-budget pre-push gate passes on `dev`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary.** Global skills live in `SorraAgents/skill/` (symlinked to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` by `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh`); the `WL-` work
  item is tracked in ContextHub's worklog and its code lands in SorraAgents
  `dev`. This mirrors the machine-hygiene epic (`WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ`).
- **Do not weaken the untracked-dir isolation work.** The filters added by
  `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` must
  stay: concurrent agents' genuinely transient `skill/<name>/` WIP must remain
  ignorable. This item removes the *permanent* untracked directory, it does not
  remove the general guard.
- **Runtime dependency is unchanged.** The skill shells out to the ContextHub
  compiled bridge (`packages/herdr/dist/pane-close-cli.js`) via
  `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE`; committing the Python copy to
  SorraAgents does not move that dependency.
- **No behaviour change** to the skill's classification, approval gate, or
  never-close guards — this is a tracking/hygiene fix only.

## Existing State

- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` exists and is byte-identical (source files)
  to `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/`; only `__pycache__/*.pyc` differ.
- The SorraAgents copy is excluded locally by `.git/info/exclude`
  (`skill/pane-triage/`) and is therefore untracked.
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` expects exactly 19 tracked skills;
  `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` enumerates the expected skill set from
  `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + ["report"]`.
- The current 140-char description limit is exceeded by the existing 234-char
  `pane-triage` description, and its `SKILL.md` uses `cd $(skill_path
  pane-triage)` + `./scripts/pane-triage.py` invocations.
- The context-budget gate (`measure_context.py --include-hidden`) currently
  passes because untracked dirs are filtered; committing the directory makes it
  count toward `skills_prose`/`total`.

## Desired Change

Choose **Option A — track the skill in SorraAgents** and make it hygiene-compliant:

1. Move `skill/pane-triage/` from untracked/excluded to tracked in SorraAgents
   `dev`, committing the same files that currently make `/skill:pane-triage`
   work.
2. Sanitise `SKILL.md` for the doc-convention and description-hygiene tests:
   rewrite the frontmatter description to ≤140 chars with a "Use when" clause
   and an action-verb first word; replace the `cd $(skill_path pane-triage); ./scripts/...`
   invocation block with `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...` forms.
3. Register the skill in `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`
   (`tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`) and update the count/total-prose
   expectations (`tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py`).
4. Regenerate `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` and add a dated bump
   note to `docs/dev/context-budget.md`.
5. Mirror the `SKILL.md` hygiene edits into the ContextHub source copy and
   document the source/deployment relationship in `docs/pane-triage-skill.md`.

The alternative (**Option B — remove the untracked copy**) is rejected: because
SorraAgents is the sole source of the global skills symlink, removing the copy
would silently retire `/skill:pane-triage` for every framework project while the
skill remains documented and referenced as deployed. Retiring the skill is a
materially larger product decision that should be raised separately if desired.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — rewrite description (≤140 chars, "Use when") and script-invocation forms.
- `skill/pane-triage/__init__.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — new tracked files (SorraAgents).
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` — update expected skill count and total-prose budget.
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — add `pane-triage` to `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — regenerate with `--include-hidden`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — dated threshold bump note.
- `.git/info/exclude` — remove the `skill/pane-triage/` entry (local, untracked).
- `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — mirror the hygiene edits (source parity).
- `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` — document the tracking/deployment model.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (highest):** committing the skill pulls in a mandatory
  `SKILL.md` rewrite, two hygiene-list/test updates, and a context-budget
  threshold regeneration. Extra opportunities (e.g. retiring the ContextHub
  duplicate, generalising untracked-dir sync) must be recorded as linked work
  items, not absorbed here.
- **Drift risk:** editing only the SorraAgents copy leaves the ContextHub source
  divergent; AC4 mandates mirroring the edits and documenting the relationship.
- **Gate-weakening risk:** the fix must not delete the untracked-dir isolation
  filters; a genuinely transient WIP directory must stay ignorable.
- **Regression risk:** the skill's runtime bridge lives in ContextHub; the
  commit must not alter the `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE` resolution or
  the approval gate.
- **Assumption:** the deployed copy is the intended artifact (not accidental) —
  supported by `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` and the active global registration.
- **Assumption:** ContextHub remains the source-of-truth repo for the skill and
  the deployed SorraAgents copy is a mirror.

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill (the skill itself; records the
  "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" placement decision).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — machine-hygiene epic; surfaced this untracked copy and
  established the global-skill → SorraAgents commit precedent.
- `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` —
  untracked-skill-dir isolation (the guard that must not be weakened).
- `WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` — shared classifier + automatic reaper (runtime
  dependency of the skill).
- `WL-0MUJW9FY5008KBTQ` — coordinate pane-triage reuse and document closure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent, evidence-based determination):** Commit the untracked
  `skill/pane-triage` to SorraAgents, or remove it? — **Answer (agent, derived
  from repo evidence):** Commit (Option A). Evidence:
  `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` states the skill is "tracked in
  ContextHub; deployed to the global skills directory as `/skill:pane-triage`";
  `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` →
  `SorraAgents/skill`, so SorraAgents is the only source of global skills; the
  producer recorded that "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" in
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`; and `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` established the precedent that
  global skills must be committed in SorraAgents. Removing the copy would break
  `/skill:pane-triage` globally. Source: repo inspection + worklog evidence.
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer confirmation):** Option A is a design decision for a
  tracked global skill, not merely a cleanup. Please confirm during review, or
  raise Option B (retire `/skill:pane-triage`) as a separate work item. Context:
  no producer response was available in this intake session.
- **Q (scope):** Should the redundant ContextHub `skill/pane-triage/` copy be
  removed? — **Answer (assumed):** No — keep ContextHub as the documented
  source-of-truth and mirror the hygiene edits (AC4); removing it would change
  ContextHub's context-budget surface and tests and is out of scope. Recorded as
  an assumption.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSM3STQ0008QUMG** – [test-failure] should have no legacy skill/ path references (Skill: cleanup) — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MR24H2VK004PAQ7** – 1a: Error Classification & Settings (tests) (completed)

# Intake Brief: Assert at the unit's observable contract — calibration for `toHaveBeenCalledWith`

**Work Item:** SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

The suite has no recorded rule for when a call-argument assertion (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`, `mock.assert_called_once_with`, `mock.call_args_list`) is legitimate and when it pins private wiring, so reviewers and agents judge each occurrence ad hoc. The churn analysis that raised this item (WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ) assumed call-argument assertions on internal collaborators were an unalloyed cost; the follow-up migration (WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM) falsified that: of 155 occurrences in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`, **148 were retained** as genuine boundary/observable-contract assertions and only **7 were migrated** to outcome assertions. The gap is therefore not "assert less on calls" but "record the retain/migrate rule, require each retained assertion to name the contract it observes, and flag the narrow remainder automatically".

## Users

- **Test author / AI agent** writing a new test — needs a decidable rule for whether to assert a call, and what to assert instead.
  - *User story:* "As an agent writing a downtime test, I want to know whether asserting `spawnFn` was called is legitimate, so I neither delete a genuine boundary assertion nor add a private-wiring one."
- **Reviewer / auditor** — needs a checklist item plus a justification convention so the judgement is auditable rather than a matter of taste.

6. **Detector tests added.** `tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py` gains unit tests for the detector: a positive case (listener-shape wiring), a positive case (assertion duplicated by an outcome assertion), and a negative case proving a boundary-adapter assertion is not flagged even when it uses `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.

# Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Goal

As a producer, I want an empirical measure of whether the largest test suites actually detect faults, so conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on evidence rather than churn proxies.

## Background

Churn and line-count metrics cannot tell us whether tests earn their keep. The top-churn / largest suites identified by the ContextHub analysis (e.g. `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `sync.test.ts`, `database.test.ts`) are mock-heavy; mutation testing directly measures whether they detect injected faults. This is the recommended follow-up before firm TDD-ROI conclusions in WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented (e.g. Stryker for TypeScript, mutmut for Python), with rationale and licensing.
2. The tool runs against at least the top three churn modules of a target project and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
3. Results are compared with test size/mock density to test the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites have lower mutation scores.
4. Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment, with explicit caveats (sampling, runtime cost, equivalent mutants).
5. The campaign is reproducible (pinned tool version, documented command) and does not regress the project test suite.
6. Runtime cost is measured and bounded so the campaign can be run periodically.

# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new

- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only

- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog

- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry

# Audit runner: Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout diagnostic hardcodes CALL_PI_TIMEOUT

`discovered-from:LP-0MV81ZIL8008RS9J` — found while auditing that item.

## Problem statement

The audit runner's Phase 2 deep-analysis failure path reports a **hardcoded
timeout** regardless of the actual abort cause, making infra stalls
indistinguishable from budget exhaustion and undermining operator diagnostics.

In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, the Phase 2 timeout branch always
raises:

```python
RuntimeError(f"Phase 2 deep analysis timed out after {CALL_PI_TIMEOUT}s")  # line ~7669
```

`CALL_PI_TIMEOUT` is the constant `1800` (line 547). This fires even when an
explicit `--timeout` (e.g. `2700`) or `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT` (e.g. `1500`)
override is in effect, because the message never consults the resolved
effective timeout (`_resolve_call_timeout`, line ~4118) or the stall detector's
resolved value (`_resolve_stall_timeout`, line ~2703).

## Observed impact (LP-0MV81ZIL8008RS9J)

Three consecutive audit runs (~60 min wall-clock each) stalled identically at
"Phase 2 deep analysis" while the shared local LLM proxy was saturated (0/3
slots free; 57k–73k-token generations in flight). In each run:

- The per-call Pi invocation did stream *something* (Phase 1 parent screens and
  verdict re-asks completed and parsed fine), but the long tool-enabled deep
  call produced no output within the stall window.
- The persisted report and the `--json` `script_failure.reason` both claimed
  "Phase 2 deep analysis timed out after 1800s" — even on the run launched with
  `--timeout 2700` + `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT=1500`.
- Because the diagnostic cannot distinguish (a) staleness/no-output vs
  (b) effective-budget exhaustion, the operator cannot tell whether to raise
  the budget, raise the stall window, or wait for proxy capacity. The audit
  had to fail closed with a fallback notice (`Ready to close: No`, non-authoritative).

## Root cause

`_run_phase2_deep_analysis` does thread the resolved timeout through to the Pi
call correctly (`_call_pi_and_maybe_log(..., timeout=timeout, ...)` →
`_resolve_call_timeout`), so overrides DO extend the call. It is only the
**failure diagnostic** that hardcodes the constant, hiding the effective values
from the operator and from the persisted report.

## Desired change

## Problem

The implement skill's Step 9 'belt-and-suspenders' post-push verification (/skill:test against the dev checkout) can resolve to a **cache hit and execute zero fresh tests**, while still looking like a green verification.

Observed end-to-end on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK:
1. implement.py finish runs the full suite (changed-scope, then --scope full) **inside the worktree**, stores green entries keyed by git state + scope in the per-repo test cache (2h TTL).
2. implement.py pushes from the worktree. In this repo the pre-push hook is a worklog-sync hook that exits 0 for worktrees (line ~80) — no test execution happens at push time.
3. The skill then says run /skill:test post-push. Because the cache key is git state + scope only, the main checkout's lookup at the same commit hits the entry stored by the finish gate. Both suite commands returned CACHED exit=0 — the final verification ran nothing.
4. Worse: the worktree environment can differ from the main checkout in ways the cache cannot see — on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK the core submodule failed to clone in the worktree ('transport file not allowed') and was populated manually; node_modules is symlinked. A green run recorded in the worktree is not proof the canonical checkout passes.

## Desired behaviour

- The post-push verification step must either (a) execute a genuinely fresh run against the canonical checkout when the push originated in a worktree (or when env differs), or (b) be made explicitly targeted for narrow changes (--scope changed --force) instead of a bare /skill:test that is cache-servable.
- The cache key should include enough environment/worktree identity that a worktree-recorded run cannot satisfy a main-checkout verification, OR implement.py finish should record whether the push came from a worktree so the post-push step knows to force a refresh.
- Keep fast iteration cheap: for narrow, well-covered changes, a forced changed-scope run is acceptable post-push evidence; reserve forced full runs for broad/refactor changes or environment drift (submodules, node_modules).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After implement.py finish pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification on the main checkout executes a fresh run (it cannot be served from the cache entry recorded inside the worktree) for the affected scope.
- AC2 — A bare /skill:test post-push no longer silently returns 'green' from a cache populated by an in-worktree finish gate without executing: either the step force-refreshes, or the implement skill's Step 9 is updated to specify an explicit scope/force invocation (and documents when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key (or its consumer logic in run_tests.py / implement.py) captures worktree-vs-main-checkout identity (e.g. git common dir, worktree path, or submodule status) so an in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted post-push runs (--scope changed --force) remain the default for narrow changes; the full forced suite runs only when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (submodule/node_modules) is detected.
- AC5 — Documented in implement SKILL.md Step 9 (and audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant) with the exact commands; regression test in tests/ where the cache layer is tested.

## Constraints

- Do not break existing 2h-TTL caching for the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification — it still needs to query cached full runs at the same commit.
- Pre-existing framework items may partially intersect: SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe), SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard + push timeout). Reconcile rather than duplicate.
- Target files (from the live symlink tree /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills -> /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill): skill/test_cache.py (cache key), skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (scope/force), skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (push origin record / verification step), skill/implement/SKILL.md (Step 9 wording), skill/audit/SKILL.md (F3/F4 notes if needed).

## Evidence

- Final /skill:test on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: both suites reported CACHED exit=0 scope=full, i.e. no fresh execution.
- Worktree push: pre-push hook exits 0 for worktrees (saw line ~80 'exit 0' in .git/hooks/pre-push); submodule 'core' failed to clone in the worktree and was populated manually.

## Problem

`resolve_pytest_command()` in `skill/test_runner.py` prefers a PATH-resolved bare
`pytest` over the interpreter that starts the runner. On a host where
`~/.local/bin/pytest` carries a system-Python shebang (`#!/usr/bin/python3`;
PEP 668 externally managed, no project dependencies), the test skill and the
audit F3 auto-run execute the suite under an interpreter that cannot import the
project's dependencies. Collection then fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` and
exit 2 even though the same tree is green under the repository's canonical
runner, which calls `python3 -m pytest`.

Observed on host `RossGameDev` against ContentCreator: 13 collection errors
(`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'` from
`.pi/skills/wiki-tts-generate/scripts/tts_generate.py`, plus
`tests/test_podcast_parts_layout.py`, `tests/test_rss_process_notes.py`) versus
2588 passed / 16 skipped via `./scripts/run_tests.sh`. The red result is cached
by git state and scope, so one such run poisons the audit-accepted full-suite
entry for that commit until a `--force` run replaces it.

## Users

- **Agent running `/skill:test`** — needs the suite result to describe the
  project's real test state, not PATH ordering.
- **Agent running the audit F3 gate** — needs a green cached full-suite entry
  instead of `missing` and a manual fallback.
- **Producer / maintainer** — needs one documented interpreter rule shared by
  every project, instead of per-repository workarounds.

User story: *As an agent running the test skill on a host whose PATH order
differs from the project's documented runner, I want pytest executed by the
interpreter that carries the project's dependencies, so that a green result
means green and the cache records a trustworthy entry.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — Resolution order is: `PYTEST_BIN`, then `TEST_PYTHON`, then
  `sys.executable -m pytest`, then bare `pytest` on PATH, then
  `python3 -m pytest`. Each candidate is used only when the earlier forms
  cannot run pytest (probed, not assumed).
- **AC2** — When bare `pytest` resolves to an interpreter that cannot run
  pytest (or cannot import the project's dependencies), it is not selected
  while an earlier candidate works, and the interpreter actually used is
  recorded in the run output and in the cache entry so the choice is auditable.
- **AC3** — Regression tests in `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` cover:
  (a) `sys.executable -m pytest` winning over a PATH `pytest` bound to a
  different interpreter; (b) `PYTEST_BIN` and `TEST_PYTHON` override winning
  over every other form; (c) the existing `which`-first and `~/.local/bin`
  fallback tests updated to the new precedence; (d) the memoised cache still
  returning the resolved command.
- **AC4** — On host `RossGameDev`,
  `python3 <skill>/test/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --force` reports the
  same green result as `./scripts/run_tests.sh` in ContentCreator, and names
  the interpreter used.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`).
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive, never weakening.** Resolution must never select a candidate that
  cannot run pytest; no suite may be silently narrowed or skipped.
- **Canonical command form is unchanged.** `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`
  stays the stable form used for cache keying and cross-consumer reuse; only
  the executable prefix varies, per the existing `executable_test_command()`
  contract.
- **Preserve the reason the bare-`pytest` rule exists.** SA-0MSQ012QG005N22S
  added it because user-site bin dirs (`~/.local/bin`) are absent from
  non-login shells. `sys.executable -m pytest` and the retained
  `~/.local/bin` fallback both keep that case working.
- **Out of scope:** ContentCreator-specific suite pinning (`.pi/test-config.json`
  → `suiteCommands`) is tracked in `OSL-0MVJOKJXK009J8ZA`. This item changes
  the shared skill only.

## Existing state

- `resolve_pytest_command()` order today: `shutil.which("pytest")` →
  `~/.local/bin/pytest` (when executable) → `python3 -m pytest`, memoised in
  `_PYTEST_COMMAND`.
- `executable_test_command()` rewrites only the executable prefix at run time.
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` asserts the current precedence,
  including `test_resolve_pytest_command_uses_which_when_on_path`.
- No `PYTEST_BIN` or `TEST_PYTHON` support exists anywhere in the tree.

## Desired change

Implement the resolution order in AC1 with real candidate probing, an explicit
per-invocation override, the selected interpreter surfaced in run output and
cache metadata, and updated tests plus documentation. Update
`test_resolve_pytest_command_uses_which_when_on_path` to the new precedence
rather than deleting it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_runner.py` — `resolve_pytest_command()`, `executable_test_command()`, probe/caching helpers
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` — new and updated regression tests
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `PYTEST_CMD`, cache entry metadata (record chosen interpreter)
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document resolution order, overrides, and cache metadata

## Risks and assumptions

- **Blast radius.** Every project that uses the skill inherits this change.
  Mitigation: unit tests cover each precedence step and the cache.
- **Probe cost.** Probing candidates spawns a subprocess. Mitigation: keep the
  existing memoisation so probing happens once per process, and probe with
  `-m pytest --version` only.
- **Cache semantics.** The cache key stays git-state + scope (interpreter stays
  informational), so a green entry produced under a different interpreter is
  still visible in its metadata.
- **Assumption.** `sys.executable` is the right default because the skill is
  started with the interpreter the agent selected (`python3 …/run_tests.py`),
  which matches the repository canonical runner.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Repository-specific pinning and dependency installation
  are recorded as separate work items, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVJE3HDF003DZ9B` — origin item; closed on creation of this item
  (discovered while verifying AC7 of `OSL-0MT47CNJE008EJGR`).
- `OSL-0MVJOKJXK009J8ZA` — ContentCreator repo-local mitigation
  (`.pi/test-config.json` → `suiteCommands`); complementary, not duplicate.
- `SA-0MSQ012QG005N22S` — original reason a bare `pytest` fallback exists.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (Map → operator, interactive):** "Where should the fix land — framework
  fix in SorraAgents, ContentCreator-only `suiteCommands` pin, or editing the
  SorraAgents checkout from the OSL work item?"
  **Answer (operator):** "A, no need to keep this item open, close as soon as
  the SorraAgents item is created." Source: interactive reply.
  Outcome: framework fix here; `OSL-0MVJE3HDF003DZ9B` closed on creation.
- **Q2 (Map → operator, interactive):** "Interpreter selection policy in
  `resolve_pytest_command()` — override → `sys.executable -m pytest` → PATH
  `pytest` → `python3 -m pytest`, or alternatives?"
  **Answer (operator):** "A". Source: interactive reply.
  Outcome: precedence recorded in AC1.

# Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

## Objective

Make `implement.py finish`'s test gate validate the exact tree the commit
will produce, and make every gate verdict self-describing (which tree ran,
whether it came from cache). A green gate must never again be produced by a
suite run against a different tree or by a stale cached result.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` runs the test gate **before** it stages and commits
(`git_commit` performs `git add -A` afterwards). Suite tests that key off the
**tracked** file set (`git ls-files`) therefore cannot see files the commit is
about to add, and the gate can report a green full-scope run for a tree that
is red the moment the commit lands. The false green is silent: the report says
"full scope, success", so no agent looks further, and the tree stays red at
the push, in CI, and for the next agent.

Observed on ContentCreator work item **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** (Ep 1 of *Inside
the Content Creation Suite*):

- `implement.py finish` reported `{"tooling": "suite", "scope": "full",
  "success": true}` and pushed commit `9c88625c`.
- A full-suite run on the same tree immediately after reported **2 failed**,
  both caused by the newly added files:
  - `test_no_podcast_episode_content_tracked_outside_documented_leftovers` —
    `podcasts/ep1-why-use-it/*` were not yet in `git ls-files`, so the
    allowlist guard passed pre-commit and failed post-commit.
  - `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` — the wiki registry was
    stale for the new synthesis page. This test reads **on-disk** files, not
    `git ls-files`, so untracked-invisibility cannot explain its false pass.
- The item was re-finished (`9f3a1f6c`) after fixing the allowlist and
  rebuilding the metadata; the suite was green at that commit
  (`2765 passed, 16 skipped`). The defect is the false green, not the fix.

Origin record: **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** (ContentCreator worklog) — full intake
brief, investigation trail, and evidence.

## Investigation findings (from the origin intake)

Two mechanisms are supported; both must be closed:

1. **Untracked-file invisibility (proved).** `git_commit` stages *after* the
   test step, and the suite runs against the loose working tree. Anything
   using `git ls-files` semantics cannot see the commit's new files.
2. **Verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree (root
   cause to pin).** Surviving cache evidence: the nearest green full-suite
   entry in the shared `.worklog/cache` (08:53, state `8e9c3ea7…`) collected
   **2751** tests, i.e. the dev tree before the episode work's test files
   existed; the post-commit red run (10:56, `f73d063e…`) collected **2781**,
   matching the committed tree. The gate's own per-worktree cache was deleted
   with the worktree, so the exact entry served cannot be recovered. Because
   the parity test reads disk, untracked-invisibility alone cannot explain its
   pass: the gate either executed against a different checkout/state or served
   a cached result recorded for a different tree.

## Desired change

1. **Temporary-index gate (operator-approved option A).** Before the gate's
   test step: copy the real index to a temp file, apply the change set to the
   copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the suite with
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
   `git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
   index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds; on failure the temp
   index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is currently **not** in `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`
   (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`), so it survives the runner's env scrub —
   this must be asserted by a regression test so a future scrub addition
   cannot silently break the fix.
2. **Verifiable verdicts.** The gate's report must state (a) the tree the
   suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
   result was served from the cache. A cached verdict is acceptable only when
   its fingerprint is the would-be-commit tree's fingerprint; otherwise the
   suite must run.

Rejected: stage-then-test with unstage-on-abort (mutates the real index,
fragile restore); `git status --porcelain`-clean assertion only (demands a
clean tree and still does not test the commit's file set).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green full-scope pass. Reproduced through the finish-gate entry point.
- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run (stale/foreign cache entries must miss).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial commit, no residual staging, and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Parity false pass explained:** the regression work reproduces the disk-reading parity case at the finish-gate entry point and records the root cause (wrong checkout / stale cache / metadata lag before staging) in this work item.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass — `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`, plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.
- [ ] **Documentation:** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (finish gate semantics, verdict provenance), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (cache fingerprint / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` contract) updated. CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship skill and excluded.
## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: no default bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.);
  guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down
  contract stay intact.
- ✗ One suite execution per gate verdict on a clean change set.
- ✗ The changed-scope development gate stays the fast path; the full suite
  stays the dev-push integration gate.
- ✗ Implemented in this repository (framework); do not edit the global install
  directly.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_guarded_suite`, gate report keys.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` / `run_cached` / `cache_dir`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, env construction
  (`subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides`).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py` —
  regression-test homes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** a temporary index changes *staged* status, which may surprise
  tests asserting on working-tree state beyond `git ls-files` (e.g.
  `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in ContentCreator's
  `test_implement_state_gitignore.py`). Mitigation: re-verify such tests in
  the regression work and document the semantics.
- **Risk:** two cache entries per state (loose vs staged fingerprint);
  accepted — correctness over hit ratio.
- **Assumption:** the parity false pass shares the gate-to-tree mismatch
  cause rather than a metadata-lag-only cause; the reproduction settles it.
- **Cross-repo note:** project-level fallout (ContentCreator's missing

# implement.py drive livelocks when phase_parent repeatedly fails to finish a child (no recovery from finishing_failed)

## Headline

`implement.py drive` can loop forever without the epic ever advancing when `phase_parent` repeatedly fails to `finish` the same non-terminal child (its abandoned worktree keeps tripping the `finishing_failed` path); drive must bound finish attempts, reconcile the child's actual state, and recover to a clean startable state instead of re-running the identical failing `finish` on every invocation.

## Problem statement

When a driven child session dies mid-work (timeout, host load), its worktree is left dirty and its item non-terminal. `phase_parent` classifies the dirty worktree as "has changes" and runs `implement.py finish <child>`; `finish` fails (build/tests red on the abandoned WIP) and resets the child status to `open` but leaves the worktree dirty. `phase_drive` then aborts the whole chain with `"Failed to finish child …"` (`finishing_failed`, `sessions_spawned: 0`), and the next drive invocation repeats the identical `finish` failure. Nothing bounds the retries or resets the child, so the epic never advances.

Observed 2026-10-19 driving epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX ("Compile an action video"): 29+ drive runs, each exiting 1 after 600–890 s with `Failed to finish child AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ`, `sessions_spawned: 0`, `parent_advanced: false` (evidence: `/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log`). Terminal children are already handled: `_classify_child` returns `skip-terminal` for `completed`/`done`/`in_review`/deleted and never reaches the worktree/finish path — so the recorded framing "drive must treat terminal children as done" is not the reproducible defect (intake Q1 → re-scoped, producer-confirmed).

## Users

- **Producers / herdr downtime dispatcher** driving epics: needs `drive` to terminate reliably and advance the epic once children are done — not burn 15 minutes per run on the same failing `finish`.
- **Epic owner / auditor** reading `drive --json` output: a truthful report that distinguishes "finished", "terminal-reconciled", and "reset for fresh session" instead of a bare `Failed to finish child`.
- **Child owner** whose session was killed: auto-recovery must not silently discard *their* progress without a recorded comment and a clean restart path.

Example user stories:

- *As a producer driving an epic unattended,* I want `implement.py drive` to terminate within one bounded cycle per child, so an abandoned dirty worktree cannot stall the epic for 29 runs.
- *As an epic auditor,* I want `drive --json` to tell me whether a child was finished, reconciled as terminal, or reset for a fresh session, so `parent_advanced: false` always means real work remains.
- *As the owner of a child whose session was killed,* I want a comment recording why my worktree was reset, so my WIP is never discarded silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Bounded finish attempts.** `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` counts failed `finish` executions per child; the same child's failing `finish` is never run unboundedly (limit configurable, defaulting to the existing per-child session cap). Unit-testable with a fake `parent_runner` that always reports `finishing_failed` for one child.
- 2. **Terminal-state reconciliation.** When a child's `finish` has exhausted its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), drive re-fetches the child via `wl show`: if the child is terminal (`completed`/`done` status or `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted), it is recorded as done (`ok`), never reset, and drive continues to the next actionable child.
- 3. **Non-terminal recovery, no livelock.** A non-terminal child whose `finish` failed is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) with a recorded comment naming the failure reason — after which drive continues and the next iteration starts a fresh session for it. `parent_advanced` reflects the true state (false only when non-terminal/blocked work genuinely remains). Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario must terminate with the epic advancing.
- 4. **Truthful report.** Per-child `children_driven` entries / failure reasons distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` (with evidence: child status/stage, failure summary).
- 5. **Terminal children never touched.** A child already in a terminal stage is never `finished`, reset, or re-spawned (regression guard; the existing `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test).
- 6. **Tests pass.** New unit tests cover: bounded-finish-attempts, finish-failure→terminal reconciliation, finish-failure→non-terminal reset+continue, terminal-child regression, and truthful reporting (drive-loop fixtures with injectable `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`). Existing `skill/implement/tests/` drive/parent tests continue to pass.
- 7. **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (and any README/wiki entries describing `drive`'s failure handling) reflect the bounded-recovery behaviour, including the recovery tiers and their audit comments.
- 8. **Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve session-per-child isolation, per-child worktree semantics, and dependency-order driving (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9); the drive recursion guard is retained.
- Never reset, finish, or re-spawn an already-terminal child; reset operations touch only the child's own worktree (never the main checkout) and always leave an audit comment on the child.
- `parent_advanced` must stay `false` while any real non-terminal/blocked child work remains; the parent advances only when every child is terminal.
- The recovery mutation (status `open` + worktree reset) is bounded and explicit — no silent discarding of WIP without the recorded reason.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `phase_parent` (~4978) — the parent-recursion loop; `_run_finish` (~5209) sets `success: false`, `finishing_failed: true`, `next_child` and returns `None` on any finish-subprocess failure; `_classify_child` (~807) already returns `skip-terminal` for terminal children.
  - `phase_drive` (~5620) — breaks the chain on `parent_report["success"] is False` (`~5765`) with no attempt accounting for finish failures and no reconciliation; `attempts` only increments on spawned sessions (`~5546`).
  - `_invoke_implement` (~4903), `_has_worktree_changes` (`~4966`), `_git_path_has_changes` (`~5909`).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status` (`~614`), `require_claimed`/`ensure_claimed` (`~664/707`) — reuse for the reset path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — spawner-command tests only; no drive-loop fixtures covering `finishing_failed` or terminal reconciliation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — documents `drive`'s session/extension mechanics; no recovery/termination semantics section for finish failures.

## Desired change

In `phase_drive` (and minimal support in `phase_parent`'s report), replace the immediate-break-on-`finishing_failed` with a bounded recovery loop per child: (1) count the failing finish; (2) when the bound is hit, re-fetch the child via `wl show` and classify with `_is_terminal_child`; (3) terminal → record as done, continue; non-terminal → comment + reset (status `open` + worktree reset to parent-branch HEAD, gated on worktree isolation checks) and continue so the next loop iteration starts a fresh session. Emit truthful per-child results. Add the discard/reset helper with an explicit audit comment and tests.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (recovery loop), `phase_parent`/`_run_finish` (failure reporting), new worktree-reset helper, `_classify_child` guard reuse.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — new drive-recovery tests (e.g. `test_drive_recovery.py`), fixtures with fake `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — status reset/finalise path for the recovery mutation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document bounded-recovery + truthful reporting.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — reinstall step (post-implementation) because the canonical source is this repo's `skill/` tree.

## Related work

- SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9 (completed) — drive all epic children to completion (fresh session per child).
- SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52 (completed) — session-per-child for epics.
- SA-0MUY9PYBD009Y7J5 (completed) — driven-child session boundary error fix.
- SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (open) — drive reports child failed on session timeout without terminal-state reconciliation: overlapping in spirit (drive does not reconcile child state), but covers the spawn-timeout path, not the `finishing_failed` path here; keep separate, cross-link.
- AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 (open, AI_Hell) — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as "has changes": the mis-detection feeds the same `has_changes → finish` entry into the livelock; keep separate (detection bug vs recovery gap), cross-link.
- AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA (AI_Hell) — seed tracker; `discovered-from` provenance; deleted per operator decision once this item was created.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1.** The reproduced livelock is entirely attributable to the unbounded `finishing_failed` retry with no reconciliation/reset; the dirty-worktree detection (`_git_path_has_changes`) is handled by AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 and is out of scope here.
- **Assumption A2.** Resetting a failed child's worktree is acceptable *only* with an audit comment and only after the finish bound is exhausted — it must never run for terminal children or children whose work landed outside the worktree.
- **Risk R1.** The worktree reset could discard legitimate WIP if a finish failure was transient (flaky test). Mitigation: bound attempts before reset; keep the failing `finish` output in the comment; prefer `reset --hard <parent-branch>` only in the child's own worktree (never `git clean` on shared paths).
- **Risk R2.** Reconciliation re-fetches child state on the slow failure path only; no added latency on the happy path.
- **Risk R3.** Scope creep into the timeout-reconciliation (SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN) or detection (AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81) items. Mitigation: cross-link rather than absorb; keep ACs focused on the `finishing_failed` loop.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Re-scope the problem statement to the evidence-based root cause (repeated `finishing_failed` on an abandoned dirty worktree), keep it as written (terminal children), or both?" — Answer (operator, interactive): A — re-scope; terminal handling kept only as a regression guard. Source: interactive reply in this intake (AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA session). Research: `_classify_child` (`implement.py:807`) already returns `skip-terminal` before any worktree inspection, so "drive must treat terminal children as done" alone would not change behaviour.
- Q2: "Recovery policy when `finish` fails for a non-terminal child: bounded attempts + reset to clean startable state (A), immediate actionable stop (B), or auto-finalise if pushed to dev (C)?" — Answer (operator): A. Source: interactive reply. Research: today `finish` on failure resets status to `open` but leaves the dirty worktree, so the next `parent` run re-runs `finish` — the exact unbounded loop (evidence `/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log`); option A breaks it while B is the status quo that livelocked.
- Q3: "Where does the change land: SorraAgents `skill/` (canonical, A), installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/` copy only (B), or both (C)?" — Answer (operator): A; additionally "once created in SA delete this work item [AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA]". Source: interactive reply. Research: the installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` is byte-identical to `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (deploy target); AGENTS.md repo-boundary rule prohibits direct edits of installed skill trees. AH-0MVFNYAOB003PDLA deleted after this item's creation per operator instruction; provenance recorded above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** – implement skill: /skill:implement <parent-id> must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain (completed)
- **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN** – implement.py drive reports child as failed on session timeout even when child completed (no terminal-state reconciliation) (open)

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: aborts, acceptable, acceptance, accounting, acs (+310 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mtlccipu0050q52, 0muwnhkqh0034dw9, 0muy9pybd009y7j5, action, actionable (+292 more)

---

## Plan

Decomposed into five test-first ordered children (test harness → bounded attempts → terminal reconciliation → non-terminal reset → docs). Vertical-slice note: each implementation feature cuts through code + tests + truthful reporting (observability) in one slice; the final docs child consolidates the reference documentation for the landed behaviour. Small effort (3.17 h expected / ~8 h recommended) and Medium risk per effort_and_risk — no approval gate was required (plan-approval-gate: Extra Large effort AND High/Severe risk only).

# Producer Actions must exclude routine workflow next steps

## Problem statement

Skill sessions end with a canonical report (helper: `skill/report`) whose
`## Producer Actions` section tells the producer what they must do. Agents
currently fill it with routine workflow progression — "Review the brief, then
run `/skill:plan`", "Proceed with implementation", "Run `/skill:audit` next" —
which duplicates the Conclusion's `Ready for <next_action>` line and, worse,
signals that the producer is blocking when nothing is expected of them.
Producer Actions should only carry actions the producer must take **to
complete the current stage**; when the only "action" is to continue the normal
workflow it must read `None needed`.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports and herdr pane titles:
  wants to know at a glance whether they are blocking a work item, and is
  distracted by reports that "ask" them to run the next skill.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: needs an
  unambiguous, copy-pasteable rule for what belongs in Producer Actions so it
  does not have to judge each time.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill finishes and the next step is just the next
  phase of the workflow, I want Producer Actions to say `None needed` so I
  don't hunt for something to do."
- "As an agent, when I finish intake and have no open question, I want to omit
  `--producer-actions` entirely rather than invent a next step."
- "As a producer, when the agent genuinely needs a decision, a missing
  credential, or an approval before the stage can complete, I want that listed
  in Producer Actions so it is not lost in prose."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `skill/report/SKILL.md` states the normative rule for
  `## Producer Actions`: it contains **only** actions the producer must take to
  complete the **current** stage (answer an open question, make a decision,
  grant an approval, supply missing access/credentials, perform a manual step
  the agent cannot), and explicitly excludes routine workflow progression
  (`run /skill:<next>`, "proceed to <next stage>", "review then continue"),
  which belongs in the Conclusion's `Ready for <next_action>`. Verified by
  document review (rule + positive/negative examples present).
- AC2: When the supplied producer-actions text consists solely of routine
  workflow progression, the rendered report's `## Producer Actions` section
  reads exactly `None needed` (the routine text is not echoed), and the
  renderer emits a single diagnostic to stderr naming the discarded text.
  Verified by unit tests covering at least: "Proceed to /skill:plan",
  "Review the intake brief and then run /skill:plan", "Next step: implement",
  and "None needed".
- AC3: Genuine blocking actions are preserved verbatim — a regression test
  asserts text such as "Answer the OPEN QUESTION in comment SA-C… before
  `/skill:plan` can start" and "Approve the remediation list in comment #4"
  are rendered unchanged (no over-eager stripping).
- AC4: Routine next-step classification is implemented once in a shared helper
  and consumed by both the report renderer and the pane-status derivation, so
  a routine next step never yields the ⚠️ `Note` pane state (`✅ Done` instead).
  Verified by unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` and
  `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py`.
- AC5: Every calling skill's final-step report template (`skill/*/SKILL.md`)
  documents the tightened `--producer-actions` contract (blocking,
  current-stage actions only; omit the flag otherwise) and no skill template
  instructs or exemplifies next-step producer actions. Verified by grep over
  `skill/*/SKILL.md` and a consistency check (test or documented command).
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Change surface is the report contract and its inputs — do not redesign the
  report layout, the `## Notes` semantics, or the Conclusion wording.
- The renderer must remain backward compatible for callers that legitimately
  pass no `--producer-actions` (already renders `None needed`).
- Classification must be conservative: rewrite to `None needed` only when
  *every* clause is routine workflow progression; ambiguous text is rendered
  unchanged (prefer false negatives over hiding a real action).
- The pane-status derivation rule (SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1: "not substantive when
  the next action is the standard next action in the workflow") must not be
  weakened or duplicated.
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` renders `## Producer Actions` from

  absent/blank (`if not producer_actions or not producer_actions.strip()`).

  producer actions and notes; `ROUTINE_TEXTS` only recognises literal

  produces ⚠️ `Note`.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` currently says only: "Producer Actions: default
  `None needed`; only list real producer actions when something is required."
  — no definition of "real", no exclusion of workflow progression.
- Every work-item skill (`intake`, `plan`, `implement`, `audit`, `test`,
  `ship`, `refactor`, `cleanup`, `code-review`, `find-related`,
  `effort-and-risk`, `resolve-pr-comments`, `machine-hygiene`,
  `agent-log-review`, `author-command`, `triage`, `report`) carries the same
  template line `[--producer-actions "<actions for the producer, or omit for
  'None needed'>"]`, which is silent on routine next steps.

## Desired change

- Add a documented classification rule + examples to `skill/report/SKILL.md`
  (what qualifies, what does not, and the mapping to the Conclusion line).
- Implement the classifier once (shared helper, e.g. a
  `is_routine_next_step()`/`normalise_producer_actions()` pair alongside
  `is_substantive()` in `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`), matching full-text
  imperative workflow-progression phrasings: optional lead-in ("next step",
  "then") + verb (run/start/begin/proceed with/continue with/review and
  proceed) + target (`/skill:<name>`, a known stage name, "the next stage",
  "planning"/"implementation"/"audit"). Return the original text unchanged
  unless every clause matches.
- Use it in `render_report.py` (both the `--json` and `wl` paths) to normalise
  producer actions before rendering **and** before `apply_pane_status()`, with
  a stderr diagnostic when normalisation happens.
- Tighten the `--producer-actions` line in every skill's final-step report
  template to the blocking/current-stage wording.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — normative Producer Actions rule, positive and
  negative examples, and the relationship to `Ready for <next_action>`.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — normalise producer actions before
  rendering and pane-status derivation; stderr diagnostic.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — shared routine-next-step classifier (single
  implementation consumed by renderer + status derivation).
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — routine-phrasing normalisation
  and verbatim-preservation regression tests.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — classifier and `derive_status`
  coverage for routine next steps.
- `skill/*/SKILL.md` (17 skills with the report template) — tightened
  `--producer-actions` guidance.
- `tests/` — optional consistency check that no skill template advertises
  next-step producer actions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False positives hide a real action.** Mitigation: all-clauses-must-match
  rule, conservative verb/target vocabulary, verbatim fallback for ambiguous
  text, and a stderr diagnostic so the author sees the rewrite.
- **Assumption — "reviewing the brief" is routine.** The intake/plan workflows
  do not gate on producer approval ("proceed automatically to the review
  stages"), so "review the brief, then plan" is workflow progression, not a
  blocking action. An explicit decision request ("choose A or B") remains a
  producer action.
- **Assumption — prose wins over heuristics.** The doc rule is the primary
  fix; the renderer guard exists to keep reports correct when an agent ignores
  the prose. Neither replaces the other.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas discovered while doing this (e.g. surfacing
  blocking actions in the pane title with a distinct state, or auto-deriving
  `--next-action`) are out of scope — record them as separate work items.
- **Wording churn across 17 skills.** Mechanical, identical replacement;
  reviewable as a single grep-verifiable change.

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via
