# implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward

> **Provenance:** mirrored from `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` (llm worklog,
> deleted after this item was created). `discovered-from:LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO`.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` rewrites the **shared** main-checkout `dev` ref (pre-push
`git merge --ff-only <child commit>`, then a post-push parent sync) while
pushing the same commit to `origin/dev`. The ref mutation and the push are not
atomic, not locked, and not verified, so two sessions finishing different
children of the same epic can interleave: a commit that was fast-forwarded into
local `dev` but not (yet) pushed becomes invisible to `origin/dev`, and the next
`finish` run either moves local `dev` past it or silently skips the whole
pre-push fast-forward, leaving the commit reachable only from its feature
branch. `finish` never checks that the commit it pushed is actually an ancestor
of the new `dev` tip, so it reports success while the commit is orphaned.

## Users

- **Agent (implementation session)** — needs `finish` to either publish its
  commit on `dev` or fail loudly naming the hash; never to report success for a
  commit that did not land.
- **Agent (parent/epic driver)** — needs the shared local `dev` to remain a
  trustworthy base, so the next child worktree is not forked from a stale or
  orphan-pinned ref.
- **Producer / operator** — needs no manual `git merge --no-ff <orphan>`
  recovery, and needs to be able to tell from the work item whether the work
  actually reached `dev`.

Example user stories:

> As an implementation agent, when a transient network error aborts my push, I
> want `finish` to leave `dev` and the remote in a consistent state so my retry
> cannot silently publish a different commit and drop mine.

> As an epic driver, I want a per-repository in-flight `finish` lock (or
> equivalent detection) so two children implemented concurrently cannot
> interleave ref updates in the shared checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — local-dev sync is remote-verified.** The pre- and post-push local
  `dev` updates only fast-forward to a commit that is already on
  `origin/dev` (or refuse loudly, naming the ref/hash, when local `dev` has
  moved since the worktree base). Local `dev` is never left pointing at an
  unpushed `finish` commit after a failed push.
- **AC2 — ancestry assertion.** After the push, `finish` asserts its own commit
  (including any rebased replacement hash) is an ancestor of the pushed
  `origin/dev` tip (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> refs/remotes/origin/dev`)
  and fails loudly, naming the commit hash, when it is not.
- **AC3 — concurrent `finish` runs are serialised or detected.** Concurrent
  `finish` runs in one repository either block on a per-repository in-flight
  lock or fail fast with an actionable message; a lock left by a crashed
  process must not deadlock the repository.
- **AC4 — regression coverage.** A test drives a failed first push followed by
  a second commit made from the older base and asserts the first commit stays
  reachable from `dev` (hermetic bare-remote + clone sandbox, following the
  existing `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` patterns).
- **AC5 — documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (post-push local parent
  sync section) and any affected `docs/dev/` pages describe the new lock and
  ancestry-verification behaviour, including the recovery path when a `finish`
  refuses.
- **AC6 — full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **The source of truth is the SorraAgents framework repo**, not this project:
  the code is `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The installed
  runtime copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` is a real copy refreshed by
  `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh`, so a source fix only takes effect after
  reinstall. This item is tracked in the SorraAgents worklog (mirrored from the `llm`
  discovery record `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO`, since deleted); the code change
  must land in SorraAgents `dev`.
- **Do not remove the rationale for the pre-push fast-forward** without
  replacing it: it exists so the pre-push context-budget gate measures the main
  checkout with the new files present (commits touching `AGENTS.md` etc. would
  otherwise be rejected by a stale checkout). Any redesign must preserve that
  property or wire the gate to the worktree tree instead.
- **Preserve the safe-skip semantics** of `_sync_parent_branch`
  (SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 AC2): never force-update, never `reset --hard` the
  shared checkout, never lose local commits, never fail a finish that already
  pushed.
- **No force-push and no rewriting of `origin/dev`.** Recovery must remain
  additive (rebase own branch, or merge).
- **Locks must be crash-safe**: `fcntl.flock`-based (kernel-released on process
  death) following `SorraAgents/skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`; no PID or
  timestamp bookkeeping. A stale lock file must not block a later `finish`.
- **Test hermeticity**: tests must use their own bare remote + clone under
  `tmp_path` and must never mutate the live checkout's refs.
- Agent test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); the full suite is
  enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` Step 5 (pre-push, `implement.py` ≈ L4273–4340): fetch
  `origin/dev`, `git checkout dev`, `git merge --ff-only origin/dev`, then
  `git merge --ff-only <commit_hash>`. Any failure raises into a broad
  `except Exception` that only logs "push will proceed from the stale
  checkout" — the fast-forward is all-or-nothing and silently disabled
  whenever local `dev` has moved.
- Step 6 pushes `<branch>:refs/heads/dev` (`git_push_to_dev` ≈ L1457). A
  generic (e.g. network) failure returns `False` → `RuntimeError` → work item
  reset to `open`; a timeout raises `PushTimeoutError`; a non-fast-forward
  raises `PushNonFastForwardError` handled by `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (≈ L3905), which rebases in the worktree and retries.
- Step 8 (`_sync_parent_branch`, ≈ L1952) fast-forwards local `dev` to
  `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`; it safe-skips on dirty/diverged/fetch-failure.
- `phase_start` Step 6.5 uses the same helper before `git worktree add`, so a
  local `dev` pinned at an unpushed commit is silently used as the base for
  every subsequent child worktree.
- No per-repository lock exists anywhere in `implement.py` (grep for
  `flock` / `.lock` returns nothing), and there is no post-push ancestry
  assertion.
- Observed incident (2026-10-25): commit `25e99ff8`
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7) was orphaned while `b0b69053` → `0c34c7d8`
  (LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI) landed; `git reflog dev` shows the local `dev` fast
  forwards to `0c34c7d8` at 02:45:53 and no entry for `25e99ff8` until the
  manual merge `f847a971` at 02:55:23 (`git merge --no-ff 25e99ff8`).

## Desired change

1. Make the pre-push fast-forward **verified and reversible**: only advance
   local `dev` to a commit whose objects are confirmed on `origin/dev` (e.g.
   push the branch first and sync afterwards, or fast-forward local `dev` from
   the remote-tracking ref and *verify* the child commit is an ancestor before
   moving), and on push failure restore local `dev` to
   `refs/remotes/origin/dev` instead of leaving it on the unpushed commit.
2. Add a post-push ancestry assertion (AC2) that names the offending hash and
   leaves recoverable state (worktree + branch retained, work item not
   advanced).
3. Add a per-repository `finish` lock (AC3) guarding the whole
   commit → fast-forward → push → sync window, with a bounded wait and an
   actionable timeout message.
4. Keep non-fast-forward recovery behaviour intact, extended to verify
   ancestry after the retry push.
5. Cover all of the above with hermetic regression tests plus a doc update.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 5
  (pre-push fast-forward) and Step 6/8 (push + `_sync_parent_branch`): needs
  verified/reversible local-dev sync, the ancestry assertion, and the
  per-repository lock.
- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev` /
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`: needs to surface the pushed tip and verify
  ancestry after a rebase retry.
- `SorraAgents/skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — reference implementation of
  crash-safe `fcntl.flock` locking to reuse (or a small sibling
  `repo_lock` helper).
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py` — new
  regression suite for AC1–AC4.
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — extend the
  existing sandbox helpers; AC1/AC2 assertions on the pre-push fast-forward.
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — extend to
  assert ancestry after the recovery rebase.
- `SorraAgents/skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the lock, the verified sync
  and the refusal/recovery path.
- `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` — reinstall step so the fixed skill copy
  is active for subsequent sessions (no code change expected).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** all `finish` sessions for a repository run on the same host
  and share one filesystem, so an `fcntl.flock` mutex is sufficient (no
  cross-host locking needed). If that ever changes, the lock becomes advisory
  and the ancestry assertion (AC2) is the remaining safety net.
- **Assumption:** `origin/dev` is the only publication path (membership of
  `main` is the ship skill's job), so verifying ancestry against
  `refs/remotes/origin/dev` is a complete success criterion.
- **Risk (regression):** removing or reordering the pre-push fast-forward can
  re-break the pre-push context-budget gate for commits that touch `AGENTS.md`
  and friends. Mitigation: keep the property explicitly under test (extend
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`/`test_implement_push_*`)
  rather than relying on the current implementation detail.
- **Risk (contention):** a repository-wide lock serialises `finish` windows;
  with the full suite deferred to the push gate the window is short, but a
  long pre-push hook still serialises siblings. Mitigation: bounded wait with
  a clear timeout message pointing at the holder, never an indefinite hang.
- **Risk (stale lock):** a crashed holder must not block the repo forever.
  `flock` is released by the kernel on process death, so a lock *file* may
  remain harmlessly on disk — tests must assert a leftover file does not block
  the next run.
- **Risk (scope creep):** fixing the false-negative push result
  (`SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX`) and the test-cache identity issue
  (`SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`) are adjacent but separate; they stay linked work
  items, not scope of this change.
- **Risk (diagnosis uncertainty):** the exact 2026-10-25 interleaving is not
  fully reconstructable from the reflog; the ACs are therefore invariants
  (verified sync, ancestry assertion, lock) rather than a single narrow fix.

## Related work

All items below live in this (SorraAgents) store. This item was mirrored from
`LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` in the `llm` worklog — the incident was observed while
implementing `llm` children, but the defect is agent infrastructure in this
repository. That discovery item was deleted once this mirror was synced.

- `LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7` — the orphaned child (cold-prefill budget enforcement);
  recovered by merge `f847a971`.
- `LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI`, `LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA` — siblings that landed while the
  orphan was in flight.
- `SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1` (completed) — "implement.py finish leaves local dev
  behind after pushing to remote dev"; introduced the post-push
  `_sync_parent_branch` this item hardens.
- `SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX` (open) — "finish reports 'git push to dev failed' when
  the push actually landed": the mirror-image failure (false negative) that
  makes an orphan indistinguishable from success.
- `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG` (open) — run_tests live-repo guard flags concurrent
  origin ref updates / push timeout: same concurrency surface.
- `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (open) — test-cache key ignores worktree identity, so
  post-push verification can cache-serve (relevant to any post-push assertion).
- `WL-0MLG0DSFT09AKPTK` (completed) — "Process-level mutex for import/export/sync":
  precedent for a crash-safe lock in this toolchain.
- `SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8` (completed) — live-repo test guard false-positives on
  concurrent agent `dev` fast-forwards: same concurrency surface in the test
  harness.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent → producer):** "The implementation lives in the SorraAgents framework
  repo (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), while the incident was observed
  from the `llm` worklog. Should the fix be implemented directly under the LP
  item, or should a mirrored `SA-…` work item be created in the SorraAgents
  store to carry the code change, with the LP item as the discovery record?"
  **Recommended:** create a mirrored `SA-…` item in the SorraAgents store —
  `implement.py start` creates a worktree from the *current* repository, so an
  LP item cannot satisfy the worktree-isolation contract when the code lives in
  SorraAgents.
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "This should be in ../SorraAgents,
  recreate there, wl sync and delete this item." Final accepted answer: this
  item (`SA-…`, SorraAgents store) carries the fix; the `llm` item
  `LP-0MVN8XWPY009AEXO` was deleted after the mirror was synced.
  Source: interactive producer reply (2026-10-25); prior answer: none.
  Research: repository layout inspection (`SorraAgents/skill/implement`,
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` real-copy install, `scripts/install_pi.sh`).
- **Q (agent, resolved by repo evidence):** "Is the vulnerable code still
  present, or has it already been fixed?" — **Answer:** still present. The
  installed runtime copy is byte-identical to the SorraAgents source; Step 5
  still fast-forwards local `dev` to the unpushed child commit, no per-repo
  lock exists (`flock`/`.lock` absent from `implement.py`), and no post-push
  ancestry assertion exists. Evidence: `diff`
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` vs
  `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (identical);
  `grep -n "flock|\.lock"` (no matches).
- **Q (agent, resolved by repo evidence):** "Does the local-dev mutation

# Prevent duplicate drive child sessions (one exclusive lock per child work item)

Migrated from ContextHub `WL-0MVNSNNLF004VPDB` (deleted after handoff). Discovered during
`WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D` (extraction of downtime-worker idle/poller modules), 2026-10-25.

## Problem statement

Two concurrent `implement.py drive <parent>` invocations can each spawn a child Pi session for
the **same** child work item in the **same** worktree, so two agents write the same files
simultaneously. Nothing serialises `drive`/`parent`/`start` invocations, and a child claimed by
another live process is indistinguishable from one that this process may resume.

## Users and user stories

- **Operator / downtime dispatcher** (runs `implement.py drive <epic>` — sometimes twice, from two
  panes or a retried cron slot):
  - As an operator, I want the second driver to refuse a child that is already held, naming the
    holder, so my in-flight child session is never corrupted.
  - As an operator recovering from a crashed driver, I want a stale holder to be reclaimed
    automatically with a logged warning, so I never have to hand-delete lock files.
- **Driven child session** (fresh Pi session implementing one child):
  - As a child session, I want exclusive ownership of my worktree for the life of my session, so
    my edits and untracked files are never overwritten by a sibling driver.

## Observed incident (evidence)

Two `implement.py drive WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7` processes (PIDs 1176064 and 1176470, started
11:52:41 and 11:52:50) each spawned a child session for the same child (`WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D`) in
the same worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVLIHY1P002WP0D-…`). Both wrote
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and the two new module files concurrently:

- one session's extraction overwrote the other's, briefly leaving a corrupt monolith (an interface
  truncated mid-declaration);
- untracked new files (`downtime-worker.idle.ts`, `downtime-worker.poller.ts`) were silently
  replaced, destroying in-progress work;
- the later session's `implement.py finish` removed the worktree under the still-running first
  session (its shell `cwd` vanished).

Sessions: A `01a172e8-0d51-702c-a5b2-db348fcc8d19` (11:52:52), B
`01a172e8-23b6-7448-87dc-3361db99a633` (11:52:58).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mutual exclusion.** Two concurrent `implement.py drive <parent>` (or `parent`, or a manual `start <child>`) invocations for one child never both enter the child's critical section: the winner proceeds, the loser reports the child as held (`action: "skipped-held"`, with `held_by: {agent, pid, session_id, started_at}`) and performs **no** worktree creation or removal, **no** status/assignee mutation and **no** file writes.
2. **Lock primitive.** Exclusion is a non-blocking `fcntl.flock` on `<worklog>/locks/child-<work-item-id>.lock`, acquired in `phase_start` **before** the work-item claim and any worktree creation/resume, and held for the holder's lifetime. The lock file records owner metadata (agent, pid, session id, started-at, token).
3. **Release semantics.** The lock is released on normal exit, on exception/abort, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (handler or `finally`); `SIGKILL`/crash release is guaranteed by the kernel. If the recorded owner pid is dead at acquisition time, the lock is reclaimed and a warning naming the reclaimed holder is logged (and surfaced in the report).
4. **Driver re-entrancy.** The driver's own subprocess chain and the driven child session it spawns (which runs `start`/`finish` for the same child id) are not falsely blocked: ownership is propagated by an explicit token (`IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, matching the token in the lock file) — never by "same pid" heuristics alone.
5. **Regression test.** A subprocess-level test runs two `phase_start`/`drive` invocations for one child concurrently and asserts: exactly one acquires, the other returns a held/skip report naming the holder, no worktree is created by the skipped one, and no file content differs from the winner's writes. Unit tests cover acquire/release, SIGTERM release, and stale-dead-pid reclamation with warning.
6. **Scope discipline.** Existing guards are preserved and not weakened: `skip-in-progress` classification, `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion refusal, the worktree placement guard, and the stranded-child finalisation ownership check.
7. **Documentation.** The behaviour, lock path, env token and failure messages are documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and the `drive` section of `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, including how an operator diagnoses a held child.

## Constraints

- No new third-party dependencies (stdlib `fcntl` only); no polling/`sleep` loops.
- No wall-clock TTL that can expire under a legitimately long child session — the kernel lock is
  authoritative, and the recorded pid only serves stale-holder diagnostics and reclamation logging.
- Lock files live under the **worklog store** (`<worklog>/locks/`), never inside the worktree
  (a worktree can be removed mid-flight).
- The lock must not interfere with the host-wide `process_semaphore` slot pools, nor nest into them.
- Fail closed: ambiguity must produce a skip-with-report, never a second concurrent writer.

## Existing state

- `phase_start` (claim at ~L3883) claims the work item unconditionally — it never checks whether
  another live process already owns the item or its worktree.
- `_classify_child` (~L819) maps a non-terminal child to `skip-in-progress`; `phase_parent`
  (~L5256) treats "in_progress + worktree present" as resumable by this process, which is exactly
  the ambiguity that produced the incident.
- `_finalise_stranded_child` (~L5957) already performs an assignee-ownership check — a precedent for
  ownership-aware guards, but assignee is a human-visible hold, not a live-process signal.
- Reusable primitives exist: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` (fcntl slot locks, kernel-released)
  and `skill/shared/queue.py` (`_DirectoryLock`).
- No lock directory or lock helper exists for per-work-item ownership today.

## Desired change

1. Add a small per-work-item lock helper (predicted new module `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py`)
   modelled on `process_semaphore`: non-blocking `flock`, owner metadata + token in the lock file,
   dead-pid reclamation with a logged warning, context-manager release on exception/signal.
2. Acquire it in `phase_start` as the first step after validation, wrapping claim + worktree
   create/resume; propagate the token to spawned driver/child processes via the environment.
3. Classify a held child as `skipped-held` in `phase_parent`/`drive` reports, with holder identity,
   and stop cleanly instead of starting a second session.
4. Cover it with the subprocess-level concurrency regression test plus unit tests, and document it.

- `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py` — new: flock-based per-work-item lock (acquire, owner metadata,
  token ownership, stale-pid reclamation warning, context manager).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — acquire the lock in `phase_start`; propagate the token in
  `_child_session_env`/`_invoke_implement`; new `skipped-held` classification and report fields in
  `_classify_child`/`phase_parent`/`phase_drive`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — new: subprocess-level two-holder regression test.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_work_item_lock.py` — new: acquire/release, SIGTERM, stale-pid reclamation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — new section: child lock, token, held-child diagnosis.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — `drive`/`parent` section: one child = one holder; what "held" means.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Re-entrancy is the main correctness risk.** The driver, its `parent`/`start` subprocesses and the
  driven child session all act on the same child id. Assumption: an explicit token in the lock file
  (plus a token in the child env) is the only ownership signal; pid equality is insufficient and
  "same session" heuristics are forbidden.
- **Signal handling risk.** A `SIGTERM` between claim and worktree creation must not leave a claimed
  item with no worktree; the handler must release and, where sane, revert the claim (mirroring

- **False-positive risk.** A lock that outlives a killed-but-reclaimed pid must not block forever;
  the dead-pid check must be tested with a recorded pid that cannot be ours.
- **Human-visible hold vs live lock.** The producer sentinel `--assignee Map` is a *scheduling hold*,

- **Scope creep (recorded, not in scope):** serialising whole `drive` invocations (a driver-level

# Refactor skill should ignore external code and packages

## Problem statement

The refactor skill's full-project scan enumerates every tracked source file
(`git ls-files`) and only filters a small fixed set of directory names. As a
result, vendored code and npm-installed packages (e.g. `packages/`,
`vendor/`, `third_party/`) that are committed to a repository are analysed as
if they were project code, producing noisy smells, spurious `REFACTOR` work
items, and misleading report counts. The skill must scan only code belonging
to the project being inspected.

## Users

- **Producers** running `/skill:refactor` (no work-item ID) against a repo that
  contains vendored or npm-installed packages.
- **Implement agents** running the refactor step inside the implement workflow
  on session changes that happen to touch external paths.
- **CI/CD pipelines** using the refactor step as a code-quality gate.

### User stories

- As a producer, when I run a full-project refactor scan, I see smells only
  from project-owned code so the report and work items are actionable.
- As an implement agent, when a session change touches a vendored/npm-installed
  file, the refactor step does not create a work item or `REFACTOR` comment for
  it.
- As a project maintainer, I can declare extra exclusions — or explicitly
  re-include a directory the defaults exclude — via `.refactor.json` without
  editing skill code.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Default external directories are excluded at any depth.** Full-project
   scans (`/skill:refactor` with no ID, and `--dry-run`) return no files under
   `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, `third_party/`, `third-party/`, `site-packages/`,
   `bower_components/`, `jspm_packages/`, or `packages/`, in addition to the
   already-excluded `.git/`, `__pycache__/`, `build/`, `dist/`, `.venv/`,
   `venv/`, `.tox/`, `.eggs/`, `*.egg-info/`, and `.worklog/`. Verified by a
   unit test on a temporary repo containing project and vendored files.
2. **`.gitignore` rules are honoured for tracked files too.** A tracked file
   matching a `.gitignore` pattern (including nested `.gitignore` files) is
   excluded from full-project scans. Implemented with
   `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z` (batch, not per-file). Verified by a
   unit test where `vendor/lib.py` is tracked but gitignored.
3. **Configuration is supported and additive.** `.refactor.json` accepts
   `"exclude": [<glob/dir>, ...]` and `"include": [<glob/dir>, ...]`; config
   excludes add to the defaults, and `include` entries override both defaults
   and config excludes for the matched paths. Missing keys preserve the new
   default behaviour. Verified by config unit tests (default-only, extra
   exclude, and re-include of `packages/` via `include`).
4. **Project-owned directories stay in scope.** Directories belonging to the
   project (e.g. `skill/`, `command/`, `scripts/`, `pi-client/`, `tests/` in
   this repository) continue to appear in full-project scan results. Verified
   by a unit test asserting their presence alongside excluded vendored paths.
5. **Session-boundary scans apply the same filter.** When a work-item ID is
   supplied, changed/untracked paths that match an exclusion (default, config,
   or `.gitignore`) are dropped before auto-fix/detection, so no work items or
   `REFACTOR` comments are produced for external code. Verified by a unit test
   passing a changed list that includes a `node_modules/` path.
6. **Report counts reflect the filtered set.** `files_analyzed`, detected
   smells, created work items, and injected comments never include excluded
   paths. Verified by asserting the returned `session_files.all_files`
   and summary counts against a fixture with mixed project/external files.
7. **Documentation and config example updated.** `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/refactor.md`, and `.refactor.json.example` document the default
   exclusions, `.gitignore` behaviour, and the `exclude`/`include` keys,
   including the note that `packages/` is excluded by default and can be
   re-included.
8. **Tests and full suite pass.** New focused tests live under
   `tests/test_refactor/` and the full project test suite passes via the test
   skill.

## Constraints

- **No new third-party dependency.** `pathspec` is not installed; implement
  gitignore handling through `git check-ignore` and config globs through
  `fnmatch` / prefix matching.
- **Backward compatible configuration.** Existing `.refactor.json` files
  without path keys must keep working.
- **Extend, do not replace, defaults.** The existing `_EXCLUDED_DIRS` entries
  remain; new external directories are added to them.
- **Single batch git call.** Gitignore filtering must not spawn one subprocess
  per file.
- **Graceful degradation.** If `git check-ignore` is unavailable or fails, log
  a warning and continue with the remaining filters; the scan must not error.
- **No behaviour change to smell detection, auto-fix, or work-item creation**
  other than scan-scope filtering.
- **Scope creep:** global git excludes (`core.excludesFile`), `.git/info/exclude`
  beyond what `git check-ignore` naturally covers, and dependency-aware
  import analysis are out of scope for this item.

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/session_boundary.py`:
  - `get_all_source_files()` enumerates tracked files via `git ls-files` and
    untracked files via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, filtering
    only by `_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` and `_EXCLUDED_DIRS`.
  - `_EXCLUDED_DIRS` currently lists `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`,
    `build`, `dist`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.tox`, `.eggs`, `*.egg-info`,
    `.worklog` — but not `vendor`, `third_party`, `packages`, `site-packages`,
    `bower_components`, or `jspm_packages`.
  - `_is_source_file()` checks only path components and extension.
  - Session scans (`get_changed_files`, `get_untracked_files`) apply no
    external-path filtering at all.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`:
  - `detect_session_files()` builds `all_files` from changed/untracked or from
    `get_all_source_files()`; it receives no config-derived path filters.
  - `_load_config()` reads `.refactor.json` but only linter/LLM/severity/smell
    keys are consumed.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py`: `RefactorConfig` has no path-filter
  fields.
- Tests: `tests/test_refactor/test_session_boundary.py` covers git diff logic
  only; there are no tests for full-project enumeration or path filtering.
- `.refactor.json.example` documents linter/LLM/severity/smell types only.

## Desired change

1. Add a path-filtering layer (new helper module, e.g.
   `skill/refactor/path_filters.py`, or extend `session_boundary.py`) exposing
   a function such as `filter_scannable_paths(paths, repo_root, config)` that
   applies, in order:
   - source-extension check (existing behaviour);
   - default external directory exclusion (extended `_EXCLUDED_DIRS`);
   - config `exclude` globs/directories;
   - config `include` overrides (re-include wins);
   - `.gitignore` filtering via one batched
     `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z` call.
2. Extend `RefactorConfig` with `path_exclude: list[str]` and
   `path_include: list[str]` fields parsed from `exclude`/`include`.
3. Thread the loaded config (and repo root) through
   `detect_session_files()` → both the full-project and session branches, so
   filtering happens once before auto-fix and detection.
4. Update the report counts naturally by filtering `all_files` before the
   pipeline proceeds.
5. Update `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/refactor.md`, and
   `.refactor.json.example`.
6. Add unit tests under `tests/test_refactor/` covering ACs 1–6.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/session_boundary.py` — extend `_EXCLUDED_DIRS`, add
  gitignore-aware filtering and config-driven include/exclude handling.
- `skill/refactor/path_filters.py` — *(new, preferred)* reusable filtering
  helper to keep `session_boundary.py` focused on git diff logic.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py` — add `exclude`/`include` parsing to
  `RefactorConfig` and defaults.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — pass config/repo root into
  `detect_session_files()`; filter session and full-project file lists.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_session_boundary.py` — extend or add full-project
  and path-filter tests.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_path_filters.py` — *(new)* focused tests for
  defaults, `.gitignore`, `exclude`, `include`, and session filtering.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document scan scope and configuration.
- `docs/refactor.md` — describe external-code exclusion behaviour.
- `.refactor.json.example` — add `exclude`/`include` keys with examples.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `packages/` is treated as an npm-installed/external directory
  by default, as stated by the producer. *Risk:* some monorepos legitimately
  keep project source in `packages/`; mitigated by the `include` override and
  explicit documentation.
- **Assumption:** exclusions apply to both full-project and session scans; this
  matches the goal of never analysing external code. If a project needs to
  refactor its own vendored fork, `include` can re-enable it.
- **Risk:** `git check-ignore --no-index` requires a git repository. Outside
  git (or if git is unavailable) the gitignore filter degrades gracefully with
  a warning; default and config filters still apply.
- **Risk:** re-including a parent directory while a child is excluded (or vice
  versa) can be order-sensitive. The design gives `include` precedence over
  `exclude` and documents the precedence; tests pin the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** requests to add import-aware dependency detection or
  per-language excludes should become separate work items, not expand this one.

## Related work

- `SA-0MQA7190K009VH6P` — Refactor Skill Core (parent feature).
- `SA-0MQA71IRP006A411` — Configuration System.
- `SA-0MTSNTZOV006P79V` — Refactor skill should run immediately when invoked
  without an ID (established the full-project scan path).
- `SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD` — Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate
  refactor need, and file work items (another full-scan behaviour).
- `SA-0MUMHH4BB000WEM9` — Add project name to the refactor report title.
- `docs/refactor.md`, `command/refactor.md`, `.refactor.json.example`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q:** What counts as "external" code? — **Answer (producer):** vendored
  packages and npm-installed packages (e.g. `packages/`). Source: interactive
  reply.
- **Q:** Should the exclusion be configurable, gitignore-driven, or both? —
  **Answer (producer):** Both. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Should project-owned `skill/` and `command/` directories still be
  scanned when the skill runs in this repository? — **Answer (producer):** Yes,
  they should be scanned. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Should the filter also apply to session-only scans? — **Answer
  (assumption, documented above):** Yes; the goal is to never analyse external
  code in either mode. Source: agent reasoning from the stated goal.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MO9W7VZX001Q6BB** – Empty audits are posted to Discord (completed)
- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** – implement.py parent ignores the do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child (open)
- **SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G** – implement.py parent ignores do-not-delegate and leaves stale worktree branches (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — matched: code, external, ignore, packages, refactor (+1 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: code, external, ignore, packages, refactor (+1 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: code, external, ignore, refactor, should

> Note: the automated matches above are keyword-based and low-confidence; the
> directly relevant precedents are the refactor-core and full-scan items listed
> in "Related work".

## Plan (decomposition)

**Decision:** no child work items. Effort is Small (~8h) and the change is a
single coherent vertical slice (one new helper module + config fields + one
call site + docs + one new test module). Splitting it into features would
produce horizontal layers rather than independently deliverable increments, so
the item is implemented directly as one slice covering every layer: code,
tests, docs, and config example.

### Execution order (test-first)

1. **Failing tests first** — `tests/test_refactor/test_path_filters.py`:
   default external directories excluded at any depth (AC1),
   tracked-but-gitignored file excluded via a batched `git check-ignore`
   (AC2), config `exclude`/`include` precedence (AC3), project-owned
   directories retained (AC4), session-boundary filtering (AC5), and
   `all_files`/summary counts (AC6).
2. **Config** — add `path_exclude` / `path_include` to `RefactorConfig`
   (`skill/refactor/scripts/config.py`) parsed from `exclude` / `include`;
   missing keys preserve current behaviour (AC3, backward-compat constraint).
3. **Filter helper** — `skill/refactor/path_filters.py`:
   `filter_scannable_paths(paths, repo_root, config)` applying, in order,
   source-extension check → extended default directory exclusion → config
   `exclude` → config `include` (re-include wins) → one batched
   `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z` call with graceful degradation
   (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4; single-batch and no-new-dependency constraints).
4. **Wire-up** — thread the loaded config and repo root into
   `detect_session_files()` so both the full-project and session branches
   filter once before auto-fix/detection and before counts are computed
   (AC5, AC6; no behaviour change to detection/auto-fix).
5. **Docs** — `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/refactor.md`,
   `.refactor.json.example`: default exclusions, `.gitignore` behaviour,
   `exclude`/`include` keys, and the `packages/` excluded-by-default plus
   re-include note (AC7).
6. **Full suite** — run via the test skill to satisfy AC8 before pushing.

### Between phases

Phases 1–5 form one slice with no independent delivery points; each phase is
verified by the tests written in phase 1. After phase 4, re-read AC5/AC6 and
confirm the session-boundary and count assertions still match the implemented
signature before the docs pass.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-26 — Plan skill run, no decomposition: confirmed ACs 1–8 each trace
  to a user story or desired-change step, validated `**Key Files:**` (7
  existing files, 2 marked new), confirmed test-first sequencing and a single
  vertical slice (no horizontal phasing), added the execution-order block
  above. No child work items created (Small effort, single slice). Stage
  advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans

Test-first slice of parent SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY (concurrent `implement.py
finish` sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev
fast-forward). This feature defines the regression contract the Lock /
Verified-Sync features must satisfy, written as hermetic sandbox tests that
are red until those features land.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC4 — regression coverage. A test drives a failed first push followed by the orphan scenario.
- A new `tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py` drives a failed
  first push followed by a second commit made from the older base, and
  asserts the first commit stays reachable from `dev` (hermetic bare-remote +
  clone sandbox under `tmp_path`, following the patterns in
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`).
- Tests assert that after a failed push, local `dev` is not left pointing at
  an unpushed finish commit — it points at `refs/remotes/origin/dev` (or a
  commit already on `origin/dev`), and the unpushed commit remains reachable
  from its feature branch.
- Tests assert that a lock file left by a crashed/concurrent `finish` run
  does not block a later `finish`, and that concurrent `finish` runs in one
  repository are serialised or fail fast with an actionable message.
- Tests run only against `tmp_path` sandboxes and never mutate the live
  checkout's refs or worklog.
- Running the new test module against the current (unfixed) `implement.py`
  fails on the orphan-reachability assertion (or is skipped with a clear
  marker) — i.e. the tests genuinely cover the defect.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py` reusing
  the `_git` / `_rev` / `_init_clone` / `sandbox` helpers already proven in
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` (extract/import them
  or a shared `git_sandbox.py` helper if importable).
- Scenario 1 (failed push then second commit from older base): simulate a
  failed `git_push_to_dev`, then finish a second commit forked from the older
  base; assert the first commit stays an ancestor of the final local `dev`
  and of `origin/dev`.
- Scenario 2 (restore-on-failure): simulate push failure and assert local
  `dev` == `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and the commit is still on the feature
  branch.
- Scenario 3 (lock): leftover lock file does not block the next finish;
  two overlapping finish windows either serialise or a clear timeout message
  is raised (no deadlock).
- Run the module via the test skill's changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py`
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py`

# Renderer normalisation with stderr diagnostic

## Goal / use case

`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` normalises producer actions via the
shared classifier (F1) before rendering the "## Producer Actions" section
AND before pane-status derivation, emitting a stderr diagnostic when
routine text is discarded (parent AC2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Producer actions are normalised via the shared helper (F1) before
  the "## Producer Actions" section is rendered in BOTH the `--json` path
  and the `wl show` path.
- AC2: Normalisation also runs before `apply_pane_status()` so a routine
  next step never yields ⚠️ `note` (✅ `done` instead).
- AC3: When normalisation discards routine text, a single diagnostic
  naming the discarded text is written to stderr.
- AC4: Backward compatible: absent/blank `--producer-actions` renders
  "None needed" exactly as today; genuine blocking actions render
  verbatim.
- AC5: All tests from the test item (T2) pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py`

## Dependencies

- F1 (shared classifier) and T2 (tests) — TDD: normalisation added to
  satisfy the failing renderer tests.

# Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates

## Goal / use case

Document the normative rule for `## Producer Actions` in
`skill/report/SKILL.md` (parent AC1) — blocking, current-stage actions
only; routine workflow progression belongs in the Conclusion's
`Ready for <next_action>` — and tighten the `--producer-actions` guidance
in all 17 skill report templates (parent AC5). Update all related
documentation (parent AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `skill/report/SKILL.md` states the normative rule: the section
  contains ONLY actions the producer must take to complete the CURRENT
  stage (answer an open question, make a decision, grant an approval,
  supply missing access/credentials, perform a manual step the agent
  cannot) and explicitly excludes routine workflow progression ("run
  /skill:<next>", "proceed to <next stage>", "review then continue"),
  which belongs in the Conclusion's `Ready for <next_action>`; the rule
  includes positive and negative examples.
- AC2: All 17 `skill/*/SKILL.md` final-step report templates carry the
  tightened `--producer-actions` wording (blocking, current-stage actions
  only; omit the flag otherwise) and no template instructs or exemplifies
  next-step producer actions — verified by the T1 consistency check.
- AC3: Related documentation is updated (code comments, README, relevant
  docs/ entries) — parent AC6.
- AC4: Change surface constrained: no changes to the report layout,
  `## Notes` semantics, or Conclusion wording (parent Constraints).
- AC5: All changed-scope tests pass and the full project test suite is verified at the dev-push gate (parent AC7).

## Key Files

- `skill/report/SKILL.md`
- `skill/*/SKILL.md` (17 templates)
- `README.md` / docs/ entries as needed


## Dependencies

- T1 (consistency check) — the check is the pass gate for AC2.
- F1 (classifier) — docs reference the real function names that land there.

# Baseline regression tests for full-suite resolution (test-first)

## Goal

Pin today's suite-resolution behaviour **before** the hidden skill-test rule
lands, so the "zero candidates → byte-identical" and "changed-scope
untouched" guarantees of SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB are enforced by durable green
tests — not only by inspection. This is the test-first slice of the parent:
it is written and committed green first; the behaviour changes in later
children must keep it green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Byte-identity baseline.** A parameterised test asserts
  `full_suite_commands(tmp_path)` equals the current resolved set for: a
  pytest-only repo, a pytest+node repo, an npm-only repo, and a repo with a
  pinned `suiteCommands` list; each result contains no command referencing
  `.pi/skills`.
- **AC2 — No-`.pi/skills` repo stays identical.** A test asserts a repo with
  NO `.pi/skills/*/tests` (the general case today, including the SorraAgents
  repo itself) resolves to the exact same command set once the F1 rule lands
  — the assertion is written against the F0 baseline and remains green after
  F1–F3 (enforced by the full suite).
- **AC3 — Changed-scope baseline.** `changed_scope_commands()` regression:
  for a representative changed file under `skill/test/`, the emitted subset
  command matches the current expectation and stays unchanged after F1–F3.
- **AC4 — Green at baseline.** The new tests pass via the test skill full
  suite before any resolver change is made.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/tests/test_suite_resolution.py` — extend the backward-compat
  class with the no-`.pi/skills` byte-identity assertions (AC1/AC2)
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope baseline (AC3)

## Summary

The implement and intake skills claim work items by setting the assignee (the
agent identity) and `status=in_progress` at the start of their run. When the
run reaches ANY terminal outcome — success, failure, or abort — the assignee
is never cleared. Under the assignee-hold convention (AGENTS_GLOBAL: "non-empty
assignee = scheduling hold (producer `Map`; clear to release)") a lingering
assignee holds the item and blocks re-dispatch/re-pickup.

The audit skill already clears the assignee on terminal verdicts
(SA-0MV98PAT7005VXXS); implement and intake must mirror that behaviour:
every terminal outcome clears the assignee so the item is released for the
producer and the next lifecycle step.

## User Story

As a dispatcher/producer, I need the implement and intake skills to clear the
assignee at the end of every run (success, failure, or abort) so completed or
released work items are never left on a scheduling hold.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — shared `StatusLifecycle` context manager
  (opt-in `clear_assignee_on_exit=True` clears the assignee on the successful
  `completed` transition; default `False` keeps other skills unchanged. The
  failure path still clears the assignee only when constructed with
  `assignee=`)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start` (claim, failure
  resets), `phase_finish` (success via `StatusLifecycle` + failure resets),
  `phase_abort` (reset to `open`)
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — `cmd_start` (claim), `cmd_finish`,
  `cmd_auto_complete`, `cmd_abort`, failure resets
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — document the
  clear-on-completion behaviour
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/` (incl. `test_phase_abort_clears_assignee.py`,
  `test_finish_no_diff_status.py`, `test_phase_start_claim.py`),
  `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py`,
  `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py`, and the parent-advance assertions in
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` / `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `implement.py finish` success path clears the assignee while still
      advancing status to `completed` / stage `in_review`
- [ ] Every `implement.py` failure reset (start/finish) and `phase_abort`
      clears the assignee together with the reset to `open`
- [ ] `intake.py finish`, `auto-complete`, and `abort` each clear the assignee
      (and failure resets do too)
- [ ] The shared `StatusLifecycle` supports opt-in clear-on-success so other
      skills are unaffected unless they request it (no silent behaviour change)
- [ ] Both `SKILL.md` files document that completion clears the assignee
      regardless of outcome
- [ ] Regression tests cover success and failure/abort outcomes for both
      skills; all tests pass
- [ ] Full project test suite passes at the dev-push gate

## Assumptions

- "Regardless of the state of the completion" = every terminal outcome
  (success → `in_review`, failure/abort → `open`) clears the assignee.
- Assignee clearing is applied only where the skill itself owns the
  transitional update (final `completed`/`open` writes), not to arbitrary
  comments or intermediate updates.

# Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review

**Headline:** The audit runner must stop re-arming `needsProducerReview` on a
passing re-audit of an item the producer has already reviewed, and must start
setting it on any failing (`Ready to close: No`) top-level audit — so a
producer's review survives a release-time re-audit while genuine failures
always reach the producer queue.

## Problem statement

On 2026-10-27 a `dev`→`main` release of the ContextHub store was blocked
because the audit runner re-flagged 14 top-level `in_review` items for producer
review. The producer had already reviewed and cleared those items; the release's
own re-audits all **passed**, and each pass unconditionally wrote
`--needs-producer-review yes`, silently discarding the producer's review.
Inversely, the failing-verdict path only flags an item when
`merge_gate_blocker` is set, so genuinely failing items never reach the
producer-review queue. The review state is unobservable after the fact because
`needsProducerReview` is a bare boolean and flag-only flips neither bump
`updatedAt` nor leave any record.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — the person who reviews and clears items before
  release. *"As a producer I want a review I have given to stay given until the
  item's content actually changes, so that I am not asked to re-approve the same
  unchanged work every time a release re-audits it."*
- **Producer, failure path** — *"As a producer I want every item whose audit says
  `Ready to close: No` surfaced to me, so that a failing item cannot sit
  silently in the actionable queue."*
- **Release gate (ship skill)** — *"As the release gate I want
  `needsProducerReview` to mean exactly 'this item needs producer attention now',
  so that the gate neither blocks on already-reviewed work nor passes
  unreviewed/unready work."*
- **Audit runner (agent)** — *"As the audit runner I want an unambiguous rule for
  when to set the flag, so that pass/fail lifecycles stay deterministic and
  auditable."*

## Target behaviour

| Verdict | Item | Prior producer review (signal present) | `needsProducerReview` after the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | yes (reviewed, content unchanged since review) | **left `false`** (do not re-flag) |
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | no (never reviewed, or content changed since review) | **`yes`** (current behaviour) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level (independent audit) | either | **`yes`** (generalise the merge-gate branch) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level, cascade-demotion-suppressed (parent-triggered re-audit of an `in_review`/`done` item) | either | **unchanged / never set** (producer decision, Q2 = no) |
| any | child (has parent) | either | **unchanged / never set** (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H) |

> **Cascade rule (producer decision Q2 = no).** A `No` produced by a
> parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item is not
> an independent review: the demotion is suppressed (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) and the
> flag is likewise left untouched. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the
> item to the producer.

Existing lifecycle guarantees are unchanged: pre-audit status/stage restore on
abort and on infrastructure failure, `updatedAt = auditedAt` on audit persist,
assignee clear-on-terminal, and the descendant cascade authorised only by a
verified `Yes`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (reviewed pass is preserved).** A passing verdict (`Ready to close: Yes`)
  on a top-level item whose producer has already reviewed it (and whose content
  is unchanged since that review) does not write
  `--needs-producer-review yes`; the stored `false` is preserved and the item is
  not re-entered into the producer-review queue.
- **AC2 (first pass still enters the queue).** A passing verdict on a top-level
  item that has never been reviewed still sets `needsProducerReview = yes`.
- **AC3 (independent failures always surface).** A failing verdict
  (`Ready to close: No`) from an **independent** audit of a top-level item sets
  `needsProducerReview = yes` regardless of whether `merge_gate_blocker` is set,
  and never clears an existing review. The single exception is the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed branch (Q2 = no): a parent-triggered re-audit of an
  already-`in_review`/`done` item leaves the flag untouched.
- **AC4 (signal is durable, auditable and content-scoped).** The review state used
  by AC1/AC3 distinguishes *"reviewed and cleared"* from *"never flagged"*, is
  recorded somewhere a later run (and a human) can inspect, and is invalidated
  when the item's reviewed content changes — so a materially changed item
  requires a fresh producer review.
- **AC5 (transitions covered by tests in the default suite).** Regression tests
  cover all four transitions — never-reviewed pass → flagged; reviewed pass →
  preserved; fail → flagged (with and without `merge_gate_blocker`); review →
  content change → pass → flagged again — and run in the default suite
  (`skill/audit/tests/`, no marker gating).
- **AC6 (children unchanged).** A passing verdict on a child item never sets
  `needsProducerReview`, and no child-item lifecycle behaviour changes.
- **AC7 (no lifecycle regressions).** The existing guarantees hold: pre-audit
  status/stage restore on abort and infrastructure failure, `updatedAt =
  auditedAt` on audit persist, assignee clear-on-terminal, cascade-demotion
  suppression, and the lifecycle readback verification.
- **AC8 (docs).** The audit skill's reference documentation
  (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` lifecycle section)
  states the pass/fail flag semantics explicitly, including that producer review
  is **content-scoped** and how a cleared flag is distinguished from a
  never-flagged item.
- **AC9 (documentation currency).** All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC10 (suite).** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Review-state signal — DECIDED: Option B+ (producer, 2026-10-28)

`needsProducerReview` alone cannot answer *"was this reviewed?"*. Two candidate
designs were carried into intake; the seed context marked Option A as preferred,
but the repository evidence gathered during intake changed the cost/benefit
picture (see *Existing state*), so the choice was put to the producer
(Appendix Q1). **Producer chose Option B+** — inference with the persisted-report
recap. Option A-lite remains a possible later upgrade but is **not** part of this
item's scope; it does not need to be raised as a dependency.

### Option B+ — infer from existing state, recap in the persisted report (no cross-repo change) — CHOSEN

At audit start, capture the item's pre-audit audit record (`readyToClose` +
`fingerprint`, both already exposed by `wl audit-show --json`) alongside the
existing pre-audit `wl show` capture. Then:

- prior audit `readyToClose == 1` **and** its fingerprint equals the current
  content fingerprint **and** the item's `needsProducerReview == false`
  → the flag can only have been cleared by a producer *after* that passing
  audit of identical content → **preserve `false`**;
- otherwise (no prior audit, prior audit failed, or content changed since the
  passing audit) → **flag `yes`**;
- `needsProducerReview == true` is never cleared by the runner.

Because the audit content fingerprint is already content-scoped (schema-2
sha256 over the item's own `title` + `description`), this option satisfies AC4's
*content-scoped* requirement with no schema change. For auditability, the runner
appends an explicit metadata line to the report it persists anyway
(e.g. `Producer review: preserved (content fingerprint <fp>)` /
`Producer review: required (reason)`), so the decision is recorded in the
durable audit record.

### Option A-lite — durable review marker in the worklog store (cross-repo; NOT chosen)

Add a nullable marker (e.g. `audit_results.producer_reviewed_fingerprint` +
`producer_reviewed_at`, or `work_items.producerReviewedAt`) written whenever
`needsProducerReview` transitions `true → false`. The audit runner then compares
the stored reviewed fingerprint with the current one: equal → preserve `false`;
different/absent → flag `yes`.

This is exact and self-documenting, but it is a ContextHub worklog change:
schema migration + repair-on-open + the marker must be written on **every**
clear path (`wl reviewed <id> false`, `wl update --needs-producer-review false`
used by the ship gate's remediation text, the ship override that clears child
flags, and any future path). It also creates a cross-repo blocking dependency
for this item.

**Cost signal:** Option B+ is a single-repo change (one lifecycle region, one
helper, tests, docs); Option A-lite additionally requires a ContextHub work
item, migration, CLI surface and its own audit. Option B+ can be upgraded to
Option A-lite later without changing this item's acceptance criteria for the
pass/fail rules. **Not chosen by the producer — no ContextHub dependency is
raised by this item.**

## Constraints

- **Do not revert the pass-flag contract.** SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 and
  SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW established that an automated pass puts a top-level item in
  the producer queue; this item refines *when*, not *whether*.
- **Never clear a review silently.** The runner may preserve `false`; it must not
  write `--needs-producer-review no` on any path.
- **Fail-safe direction.** When the review signal is ambiguous or unavailable
  (e.g. `wl audit-show` fails, legacy fingerprint-less audit), the runner must
  fall back to **flagging** (`yes`) — a spurious review request is a nuisance; a
  silently discarded review gate is a release-safety defect.
- **Bias to fewer `wl` calls.** No new per-item `wl` invocation on the hot path
  where the existing freshness gate already fetched the audit record; the
  forced path (`--force` / `--refresh-audits`) adds exactly one `wl audit-show`.
- **Children remain exempt** from the flag (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H).
- No new user-facing CLI flags; no change to how a producer clears the flag.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the passing-verdict lifecycle
  (~13576–13600) appends `["--needs-producer-review", "yes"]` for every
  top-level item with no reference to prior review state; the failing-verdict
  lifecycle (~13626–13660) adds the same flag **only** under
  `if ctx.merge_gate_blocker:` in the demotion branch.
- The runner already fetches everything needed for the decision: `wl show` at
  ~10247 yields `ctx.wi` (including `parentId` and `needsProducerReview`), and
  the pre-audit `original_status` / `original_stage` capture (~10238–10256) is
  the natural home for a pre-audit audit-record capture.
- `_check_audit_freshness` (~2085–2160) already runs `wl audit-show <id> --json`
  on the non-forced path and compares the stored v2 content fingerprint with the
  recomputed one — the same data Option B+ needs. The forced path
  (`--force`, `--refresh-audits`, batch drains) bypasses the gate, so an explicit
  capture is required there.
- `audit_results` (ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts` ~305–315) already stores
  `ready_to_close`, `audited_at`, `fingerprint`; `wl audit-show --json` exposes
  `fingerprint` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts`). `wl list --json` additionally
  emits a recomputed `currentFingerprint` via `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`
  (parity-tested against the Python algorithm).
- The audit content fingerprint is **item-data-only** (schema 2: sha256 over
  `title` + `description`) — comments and flag flips do not contribute, so a
  review-clear or a comment cannot invalidate a stored fingerprint.
- ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts` is a flag-only flip; the ship gate's
  remediation guidance (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` ~506–530) and
  `run-release.js` (~668–710) clear flags with `wl update <id>
  --needs-producer-review false`. A durable marker (Option A-lite) would have to
  hook **all** of these, not just `wl reviewed`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` lives in **ContextHub**, not SorraAgents (the seed's Key
  Files section lists it without a repo; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` are the SorraAgents-side surfaces).
- The flag-only-flip contract ("flips of `needsProducerReview` do not bump
  `updatedAt`", `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` ~260) means `updatedAt` **cannot** be used
  as a review timestamp — it is bumped by the audit persist itself.
- Current behaviour is pinned by tests that must be updated with the fix:
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (pass-with-hold cases at
  ~239, ~306, ~521, ~544), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` ~436
  (cascade pass still flags), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`
  (fail-flag cases ~523–700).
- The mock harness `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py`
  (`stateful_wl_side_effect`) deliberately passes `audit-show` through untouched
  — it needs a pre-audit audit-record knob so the new rules can be exercised.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

1. **Capture pre-audit audit state** next to the existing pre-audit `wl show`
   capture: `prior_audit = {readyToClose, fingerprint, auditedAt}` (reuse the
   freshness gate's fetch on the non-forced path; one `wl audit-show` otherwise).
   Capture failure ⇒ treat as "no prior audit" (fail-safe → flag).
2. **Add one predicate** (e.g. `_producer_review_preserved(wi, prior_audit)`)
   implementing the chosen signal from the *Review-state signal* section, with a
   single documented truth table. Pure function, unit-testable without the model.
3. **Passing branch**: keep `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level items
   **unless** the predicate holds, in which case append nothing (preserve the
   stored `false`). Log the decision (stderr + the persisted report line) with the
   reason and fingerprint. The rule is identical for items already at a terminal
   `done` stage (those keep their stage and only gain/lose the flag).
4. **Failing branch (independent `No`)**: emit `--needs-producer-review yes` for
   every top-level `No` verdict — merge-gate-blocked *and* ordinary `No` — keeping
   the existing merge-gate behaviour and adding the general case. Never emit `no`.
   This applies **only** when `_cascade_suppress_demotion` is false (see step 5).
5. **Unchanged branches**: infrastructure-failure restore and cascade-demotion
   suppression keep the flag untouched (no set, no clear) — record this explicitly
   in comments so a future edit does not "helpfully" flag on a timeout or a

6. **Children**: no change (no flag on pass, existing behaviour elsewhere).

8. **Tests** (default suite, `skill/audit/tests/`): extend the mock harness with a

   regression, merge-gate parity, the cascade-suppressed-`No`-does-not-flag case

   flag lifecycle / content-scoped review" section) and
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85 lifecycle text), including the chosen option
   and the fail-safe rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — passing-verdict lifecycle (~13576–13600), failing-verdict lifecycle (~13626–13660), pre-audit capture (~10238–10256), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` (~2085–2230). - `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — report persistence; needs the "Producer review: preserved/required" metadata line (Option B+).
- `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py` — mock harness; needs a prior-audit/`audit-show` knob.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_review.py`, `test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — pinned expectations to update plus the new transition tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision 1 (cascade, producer Q2 = no).** A `No` verdict produced by a
  parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item does
  **not** set the flag — the flag follows the demotion: suppressed demotion ⇒ no
  flag. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the item to the producer. Note
  this deliberately narrows the merge-gate branch too: a cascade-suppressed
  merge-gate `No` does not flag (the next independent audit re-surfaces it).
- **Assumption 1 (infrastructure failure).** An infrastructure-failure restore
  leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched (neither set nor cleared): a model
  timeout must never manufacture a producer-review request nor discard a review
  (producer Q3 = yes).
- **Assumption 2 (fail-safe).** Any ambiguity in the review signal resolves to
  *flag* (`yes`), never to *preserve* (`false`).
- **Assumption 3 (scope).** Only the audit runner's lifecycle writes the flag;
  the ship gate's own clearing/escalation paths (`check-audit-gate.js`,
  `check-final-validation.js`, `run-release.js`) are out of scope and unchanged.
- **Risk: derived signal (Option B+).** Without a stored review marker, a
  human cannot see *when* the producer reviewed, only that the flag is `false`
  over an unchanged passing audit. Mitigation: the persisted report line records
  the decision + content fingerprint, and Option B+ upgrades cleanly to Option
  A-lite later.
- **Risk: stale fixture expectations.** The current suite pins the unconditional
  flag in ≥6 places; a rushed edit could "fix" the tests instead of the
  behaviour. Mitigation: each test states which of AC1–AC6 it pins.
- **Risk: extra `wl` latency.** Mitigation: reuse the freshness gate's fetch;
  at most one added `wl audit-show` per forced audit.
- **Accepted edge (Option B+).** A flag cleared by an automated override rather
  than a human (the ship gate's child remediation, or the post-release close
  step) is indistinguishable from a human review. Both are intentional clears and
  preserving them is the correct outcome, so no attempt is made to tell them
  apart.
- **Risk: cascade failures are surfaced later, not immediately (Q2 = no).** A
  failing cascade re-audit no longer flags, so a genuine problem found only by a
  cascade pass reaches the producer at the next independent audit. Mitigation:
  the cascade run already prints its suppression notice to stderr and the
  persisted report keeps the `No` verdict visible on the item.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Related improvements spotted during implementation
  (e.g. a producer-review audit trail across the whole worklog, a
  `wl review-history` command) are recorded as separate work items, not folded
  into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (no parent) *(completed)*: narrowed the flag to top-level
  items; its child exemption is preserved by AC6.

  verdicts *(completed)*: introduced the unconditional pass flag this item
  refines.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item ready to close *(completed)*: the original contract.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** — Update documentation for producer-review gating
  *(completed)*: the docs this item extends.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** — merge-gate fail-closed flag on integration failure:
  the `merge_gate_blocker` branch generalised by AC3.
- **SA-0MUJAPC680078396** — cascade-audit demotion suppression (relevance:
  Decision 1 — the flag follows the demotion).
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT / SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** — audit content fingerprint and
  the item-data-only (v2) formula: the content-scoping mechanism AC4 reuses.

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** – Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (no parent) (completed)
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** – Update documentation for producer-review gating (completed)
- **SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5** – Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes' verdicts (revert assignee-hold producer marking, keep assignee clear-on-terminal) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~220 further tokens)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~215 further tokens)

## Evidence (reproduction)

1. Create a top-level item and audit it to a passing verdict → `needsProducerReview = yes` (AC2 behaviour).
2. `wl reviewed <id> false` (or `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) → flag clears, `updatedAt` unchanged.
3. Re-audit the unchanged item to a passing verdict (or run the ship gate's `--refresh-audits`) → observed: `needsProducerReview` flips back to `yes` with `updatedAt == auditedAt`. Expected after the fix: stays `false`.

Inspect the flag at any point with:

```bash
wl show <id> --json | jq '{needsProducerReview: .workItem.needsProducerReview, updatedAt: .workItem.updatedAt}'
wl audit-show <id> --json | jq '.audit | {readyToClose, auditedAt, fingerprint}'
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py check-freshness <id>   # read-only probe
```

Observed on 2026-10-27 for WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P, WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8,
WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6, WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66, WL-0MVMSE2S0006L56D, WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0,
WL-0MVMSE5LN003KCPQ, WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX, WL-0MVOTIJ2U000JI44,
WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG, WL-0MVPRZU0A000TSWD, WL-0MVM92MZ50075E6B.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (review-state signal, blocking):** *"`needsProducerReview` alone cannot
  answer 'was this reviewed?'. Choose the review-state signal: (a) **Option B+** —
  infer from the stored passing audit + unchanged content fingerprint, and recap
  the decision in the persisted report (no cross-repo change, ~1 day); (b)
  **Option A-lite** — add a durable `producer_reviewed_at` + fingerprint marker
  written on every `true → false` transition (exact, but a ContextHub schema +
  CLI change, raising a cross-repo dependency and blocking this item)."*
  **Recommended:** Option B+ — the v2 content fingerprint already stored on
  `audit_results` makes the inference content-scoped, so AC4 is met without a
  worklog schema change or a cross-repo blocker; Option A-lite remains a clean
  later upgrade.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "b+" — Option B+ chosen.** Option A-lite is
  rejected for this item: no ContextHub schema/CLI change and no cross-repo
  dependency. Research evidence: inspected `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  lifecycle + `_check_audit_freshness`, ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts`,
  `src/persistent-store.ts` `audit_results`, `src/commands/audit-result.ts`,

- **Q2 (cascade behaviour):** *"Should a `No` verdict from a parent-triggered

  **Recommended:** Yes — demotion suppression protects workflow position, the

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs
- Failing commit: d639d615
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
transcription failed: No module named 'numpy' — 9 unit subtests fail; the worker imports numpy at pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:117 and the host python3 (/usr/bin/python3, 3.12, no venv) cannot import it. pytest + node tests/node + node tests/cli all pass; only tests/unit fails.
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout d639d615`
2. Run the failing test through the test skill (changed scope, unit type) — or directly `node --test tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` from a non-agent shell
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

Reproduce without leaving the current checkout (numpy-free simulation): any interpreter whose `import numpy` fails, e.g. `python3 -S -c "import numpy"` (verified on the planning host: plain `python3` imports numpy 2.5.1 from the user site-packages, `python3 -S` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`).

## Root Cause Analysis (plan phase)

- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:115` `pcm_to_float32()` performs a lazy `import numpy as np` (`:117`); it is called from `TranscriptionSession` on every partial/final transcription (`:194`).
- The import is undeclared and unchecked: nothing validates numpy at `start`, so a numpy-free interpreter surfaces it only mid-stream as `{"type": "error", "message": "transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'"}` (`:334`, `:344`) — which fails 9 lifecycle subtests instead of producing an actionable startup error the way a missing `faster_whisper` does (`:268`–`:283`).
- The harness (`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs:58`–`:70`) is deliberately hermetic for `faster_whisper` (stub module injected through `PYTHONPATH`) but injects nothing for numpy, and spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` (`:31`) — i.e. whatever host interpreter is on `PATH`. Green on this host only because the developer's `python3` happens to carry numpy via the user site-packages.
- The documented contract is wrong: `docs/dev/voice-input.md:256`–`264` states the worker tests need no dependency install ("inject a stub `faster_whisper` module via `PYTHONPATH` … without the dependency installed"). numpy is a real, transitive hard requirement of faster-whisper, so it is present in any environment where the worker can do useful work — it is simply not declared, not checked, and not stubbed.
- Related prior art (not a duplicate — that item's scope is `wl sync` identity/purge): SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC comment 2026-10-15 records the same red suite on a host whose "system python3 lacks numpy", where "no passwordless sudo + PEP 668 externally-managed" made installing it impossible. The environment cannot be fixed from the repo, so harness hermeticity is the only durable fix.

## Key Files:

- pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py
- tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs
- docs/dev/voice-input.md

## Minimal Implementation:

1. Test-first (red): add a minimal `numpy` stub module to the temp stub directory created in the test's `before()` hook, exposing just what the worker uses (`frombuffer(data, dtype="<i2")` → an object with `.astype("float32")` and float division returning a sequence that supports `len()`), and add a subtest that runs the worker against a stub dir whose `numpy.py` raises `ImportError` and asserts an actionable `error` message at `start` (not a mid-stream `transcription failed`).
2. Worker: hoist the numpy availability check next to the existing `faster_whisper` import handling so a missing numpy produces the same actionable `error` at `start` (`:268`–`:283`), keeping the numpy-free import path for module import/doctor use.
3. Docs: correct `docs/dev/voice-input.md` — the test table plus the stub note must say both `faster_whisper` and `numpy` are stubbed, and numpy is listed as a runtime requirement of the worker.
4. Verification: run the changed-scope tests through the test skill; confirm the worker suite is green with a numpy-free interpreter and that no subtest is skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` passes on an interpreter that cannot import numpy: the harness supplies a stub numpy through the same `PYTHONPATH` stub directory used for `faster_whisper`, so all lifecycle subtests pass (no skips, no `.skip`) with no site-packages numpy available.
2. A missing numpy is reported as an actionable `error` message at `start` (same treatment as a missing `faster-whisper`), and a subtest covers it — the worker no longer emits `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` mid-stream.
3. `docs/dev/voice-input.md` documents the numpy runtime requirement and that the unit tests stub both `faster_whisper` and `numpy` (documentation matches the harness).
4. The full project test suite passes with the changes (dev-push gate green), and the fix is validated on the affected host as well as locally.

## Assumptions

- A1: Hermeticity is fixed in the test harness rather than by removing numpy from the worker. numpy is a hard transitive dependency of faster-whisper and `pcm_to_float32()` is the hot path for every partial/final transcription, so replacing it with a pure-Python conversion would add production risk for no user-visible benefit.
- A2: Extending the existing "missing dependency → actionable error, not a crash" behaviour from `faster-whisper` to numpy is treated as in-scope for this triage item (it is the message that made this failure look like a transcription bug); it is a few lines beside the existing handler. If the producer prefers the strictly minimal stub-only fix, AC2 can be dropped without affecting ACs 1, 3 and 4.
- A3: No environment remediation (installing numpy via sudo/pip) is part of this item — SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC documents that the affected host has no passwordless sudo and PEP 668 blocks it.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun the test through the test skill once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue. (Not flaky: deterministic on any numpy-free interpreter.)

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- Voice-input design: docs/dev/voice-input.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the failure reproduce on the planning host? Answer (planning agent, 2026-10-28): not directly — plain `python3` imports numpy 2.5.1 from `~/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages`. Evidence: `python3 -c "import numpy"` succeeds, `python3 -S -c "import numpy"` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. The failure is environment-dependent and always reproducible when the spawned interpreter has no numpy, which is why AC1 requires the harness to supply it.
- Q: Is numpy required in production? Answer (planning agent, from `faster-whisper` dependency semantics and the worker code): yes — faster-whisper itself depends on numpy and `pcm_to_float32()` feeds `WhisperModel.transcribe()`. Evidence: `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:115`–`119`, `:194`.
- Q: Is this a duplicate of prior work? Answer: no. `wl search "whisper worker numpy"` returned only SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC, whose ACs cover `wl sync` GitHub identity authorisation and history purge; it mentions this suite only as a blocked-push deviation. Evidence: `wl show SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC --json`.
